The problem: available text does not identify a training corpus An LLM learns from the text supplied to its training pipeline. A filename alone does not identify that text: two files named train.txt can contain different bytes. A source can also change between revisions. Even the intended text is an incomplete corpus record if its source revision, license text or attribution has been lost. Before filtering or tokenizing, we need to connect the selected text to its documented origin and check that the supplied bytes match that selection. The same check should work whether those bytes arrive from a file, an HTTP client or another reader, and whether the verified bundle is kept in memory, files or another store. How bytes travel and where they are kept do not change which content was selected. This chapter implements that content boundary. Verification does not clean the text, establish privacy, grant legal permission or measure its usefulness for training.
Start with a complete, tiny corpus bundle The example uses course-authored test bytes, not a downloaded training dataset. A payload is one byte sequence included in the bundle. A content ID is its logical name within the selected record, not a filename or a URL. Content ID | Role in this fixture | Exact bytes as a Rust literal | Byte count train | Raw training source | b"abc" | 3 validation | Raw held-out source | b"hello
" | 6 license | Shared license text | b"fixture-only
" | 13 attribution | Shared attribution text | b"course-authored fixture
" | 24 In these literals, 
 represents one newline byte. The raw text contains 3+6=9 bytes. The complete payload contains 3+6+13+24=46 bytes, excluding the manifest introduced below. Both source records refer to the same license and attribution payloads; shared bytes are inventoried once. The fixture’s license identifier is LicenseRef-Course-Test-Only, and its redistribution labels are not-approved. These describe the synthetic record, not permission for a real corpus or a trained model. The held-out source is raw input; its name does not define the final validation or test split.
The solution: select the record, then verify its content A manifest records the bundle. Each payload entry supplies a content ID, role, media type, exact byte count and SHA-256 digest. Each source record names the corresponding content ID, source revision, provenance reference, license and attribution. The provenance reference is descriptive evidence; it need not be a URL and is not an instruction to fetch anything. The caller must select the expected record independently of the candidate being checked. Rust’s DatasetPolicy stores that selection. Copying an untrusted candidate into the expected policy would check only its internal consistency, not whether it was the intended corpus. The verifier cannot make the caller’s provenance claims true merely by matching them. For this tiny example, the selected record contains 2 sources and 4 payloads. The reusable verifier does not require those counts. Other selections can name different numbers of sources, share metadata or include additional payloads. The manifest has one canonical representation: compact UTF-8 JSON, object keys sorted by their UTF-8 bytes, payload entries sorted by the UTF-8 bytes of their content IDs, source entries sorted by the UTF-8 bytes of their source IDs, and exactly one final newline. An incoming manifest with different formatting or ordering is rejected, not silently rewritten. This fixes the exact bytes used for identity: \mathrm{artifact\_id}=\operatorname{SHA256}(\mathrm{canonical\_manifest\_bytes})
What the identity formula means Here \mathrm{canonical\_manifest\_bytes} is the complete canonical record, including payload digests and provenance. \operatorname{SHA256} maps those bytes to a 256-bit digest. \mathrm{artifact\_id} is that digest, displayed as 64 hexadecimal characters. It identifies a record; it is not a signature or a permission, privacy or quality certificate. Payload bytes affect the identity through their recorded counts and digests. The verifier must still read the actual payloads. Hashing a manifest does not prove that its claimed content exists. Rust identifies the complete corpus record by hashing its exact canonical manifest bytes; the payloads still require verification. rust/crates/llm-from-scratch/src/artifact/canonical_manifest.rs#dataset-artifact-identity pub fn artifact_id( manifest: &DatasetArtifactManifestV2, ) -> Result<ArtifactDigest, AcquisitionError> { Ok(sha256(&canonical_manifest_bytes(manifest)?)) }
Verify supplied bytes without choosing their transport The content verifier performs three checks in order: Validate the candidate manifest’s structure and require exact agreement with the independently selected policy, including its provenance and producer identifiers. Require the provider’s logical inventory to match the selected payload IDs exactly. A missing, extra or duplicate ID causes refusal before payloads are opened or destination staging is created. Read every selected payload through standard Rust I/O. Compare its observed length and digest with its selected entry. Accept the bundle only after every payload passes. AssetSource supplies the logical inventory and a standard Read reader for each selected payload. The provider decides how to obtain those bytes. Filesystem path safety and HTTP response handling belong to the relevant adapter or library, not to the content checks. A future provider can implement the same interface without adding a new retrieval mode to the verifier. verify_payload_into uses standard I/O to stream into a writer while the course code counts bytes and updates the digest. For a selected 3-byte payload, it observes at most 4 bytes: the fourth distinguishes a complete 3-byte stream from a longer stream with the same prefix. That excess byte is not written to the destination. A short stream fails with Size; so does an overrun. Equal-length content with the wrong digest fails with Hash. A reader or writer failure is Io, not successful end of input. Rust compares streamed content with the selected byte count and digest, observes one possible excess byte, and keeps any failed write provisional. rust/crates/llm-from-scratch/src/artifact/inventory.rs#bounded-payload-verification struct CheckingWriter<'a, W: ?Sized> { sink: &'a mut W, hash: Sha256, bytes: u64, limit: u64, oversized: bool, } impl<W: Write + ?Sized> Write for CheckingWriter<'_, W> { fn write(&mut self, chunk: &[u8]) -> std::io::Result<usize> { let retained = (chunk.len() as u64).min(self.limit - self.bytes) as usize; self.sink.write_all(&chunk[..retained])?; self.hash.update(&chunk[..retained]); self.bytes += retained as u64; if retained != chunk.len() { self.oversized = true; return Err(std::io::Error::new( std::io::ErrorKind::InvalidData, "content exceeds selected size", )); } Ok(retained) } fn flush(&mut self) -> std::io::Result<()> { self.sink.flush() } } /// Standard I/O performs streaming and propagates backend failures. The course /// compares the selected length and digest, and never writes the excess byte /// used to distinguish a true EOF from a same-prefix oversize stream. /// The sink can contain an unverified prefix on failure. Its owner must keep /// that prefix private; this function does not roll back arbitrary writers. pub fn verify_payload_into<R: Read + ?Sized, W: Write + ?Sized>( expected: &PayloadEntry, reader: &mut R, sink: &mut W, ) -> Result<VerifiedPayload, AcquisitionError> { let read_limit = expected .bytes .checked_add(1) .ok_or(AcquisitionError::Size)?; let mut checked = CheckingWriter { sink: &mut *sink, hash: Sha256::new(), bytes: 0, limit: expected.bytes, oversized: false, }; let copied = std::io::copy(&mut reader.take(read_limit), &mut checked); if checked.oversized { return Err(AcquisitionError::Size); } copied.map_err(|_| AcquisitionError::Io)?; if checked.bytes != expected.bytes { return Err(AcquisitionError::Size); } let digest = format!("{:x}", checked.hash.finalize()); if digest != expected.sha256 { return Err(AcquisitionError::Hash); } sink.flush().map_err(|_| AcquisitionError::Io)?; Ok(VerifiedPayload { id: expected.id.clone(), bytes: expected.bytes, sha256: digest, }) } pub fn verify_payload<R: Read + ?Sized>( expected: &PayloadEntry, reader: &mut R, ) -> Result<VerifiedPayload, AcquisitionError> { verify_payload_into(expected, reader, &mut std::io::sink()) } SHA-256 and JSON syntax use supporting libraries. Course Rust owns record consistency, canonical ordering, selected-policy agreement, logical inventory and the comparisons that decide admission. Keep incomplete content out of the published bundle AssetStore creates a private stage with standard Write writers. A writer may contain an unverified prefix when verification fails. Such bytes must remain unpublished; the caller must not treat them as an admitted payload. acquire_bundle verifies each payload, finishes it in the private stage, and calls publish only after the entire bundle passes. The storage adapter owns atomic publication, durability and cleanup. The content algorithm does not assume a directory layout, reserved manifest filename or database protocol. The example uses a memory store. Its failed replacement leaves the prior bundle unchanged and publishes no partial candidate. This demonstrates the admission order and this store’s behavior, not crash durability for every possible storage backend. An adapter must publish a complete bundle or none of it; a storage error after publication may leave a complete bundle visible and must not be described as proof of rollback. Rust stages selected payloads privately and requests publication only after every length and digest check succeeds; the store owns atomic visibility and durability. rust/crates/llm-from-scratch/src/artifact/acquisition.rs#content-admission pub fn acquire_bundle<S: AssetSource, D: AssetStore>( manifest: &DatasetArtifactManifestV2, policy: &DatasetPolicy, source: &mut S, destination: &mut D, ) -> Result<VerifiedBundle, AcquisitionError> { admit_inventory(manifest, policy, source)?; let manifest_bytes = canonical_manifest_bytes(manifest)?; let mut stage = destination.stage(manifest)?; let mut verified = Vec::with_capacity(manifest.payload.len()); for expected in &manifest.payload { let mut reader = source.open_payload(expected)?; let mut writer = stage.create_payload(expected)?; let payload = verify_payload_into(expected, &mut reader, &mut writer)?; stage.finish_payload(expected, writer)?; verified.push(payload); } let proof = bundle_proof(manifest, policy, verified)?; stage.publish(&manifest_bytes, &proof)?; Ok(proof) } Two changes that expose the boundary Replacing b"abc" with b"abd" preserves the training payload’s 3-byte length. A byte-count check accepts the replacement, but the full verifier returns Hash. This identifies a content mismatch, not what either text would teach an LLM. For a separate deliberate selection, change attribution to b"course-authored fixture v2
". Its payload entry now records 27 bytes and a different digest. The source records still refer to the same logical attribution ID; the raw text digests remain unchanged. The new complete payload totals 49 bytes, and its canonical manifest has a different identity. The original policy refuses this variant until the caller independently selects the new record; changing supplied metadata does not authorize itself. replay_bundle reads a canonical manifest, checks the selected artifact identity and verifies every currently supplied payload again. It has no destination-writing interface. Matching an old identity alone would not detect payload bytes changed afterward. The executable prints a report with scope synthetic-offline-fixture, including all payload counts and digests, the attribution comparison, complete replay and the preserved prior bundle. These are checked toy results, not acquisition of a training dataset. The synthetic Rust report distinguishes corpus-record identity, verified payload bytes, complete replay and the memory store's failed-replacement result. rust/demos/ch41-governed-corpus-acquisition/src/lib.rs#governed-report Ok(serde_json::json!({ "artifact_id": verified.artifact_id(), "artifact_manifest_bytes": canonical_manifest_bytes(&manifest)?.len(), "attribution_variant_artifact_id": artifact_id(&variant)?.as_hex(), "checks": { "attribution_change_changes_bundle_identity": artifact_id(&manifest)? != artifact_id(&variant)?, "attribution_change_preserves_raw_digests": manifest.payload.iter().filter(|entry| entry.role.starts_with("raw-")).all(|entry| variant.payload.iter().any(|other| other.id == entry.id && other.sha256 == entry.sha256)), "complete_bundle_replay_identity": replay == verified, "failure_preserves_prior_bundle": refusal == AcquisitionError::Hash && prior.bundles == last_good, "same_size_wrong_bytes_refusal": corrupt.to_string(), "size_only_contrast_accepts_abd": size_only_accepts(train.bytes, b"abd") }, "inventoried_payloads": verified.payloads().len(), "logical_sources": manifest.sources.len(), "payloads": verified.payloads().iter().map(|entry| serde_json::json!({"bytes":entry.bytes(),"id":entry.id(),"sha256":entry.sha256()})).collect::<Vec<_>>(), "privacy_quality_or_redistribution_approval": false, "raw_bytes": 9, "schema_version": 2, "scope": policy.evidence_kind(), "total_payload_bytes": verified.total_bytes() })) Run the demo from the repository root, the directory containing course, with Docker installed and running. Set COURSE_CORPUS=false because this example uses only its tiny built-in inputs, not the optional large corpus. If the workspace image is absent, the wrapper first builds it using network access for dependencies; the demo itself then runs with network access disabled: COURSE_CORPUS=false ./course run cargo run --offline --locked -p ch41-governed-corpus-acquisition The command prints the JSON report described above, with 2 logical sources, 4 verified payloads, 9 raw bytes and 46 total payload bytes. Its same_size_wrong_bytes_refusal is Hash, and failure_preserves_prior_bundle is true. The executable runs the course-authored offline corpus fixture and prints its checked report; it does not download a corpus. rust/demos/ch41-governed-corpus-acquisition/src/main.rs#offline-acquisition-example fn main() -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> { // The executable has no HTTP transport and no production acquisition mode. let report = run_fixture()?; println!("{}", serde_json::to_string_pretty(&report)?); Ok(()) }
History: preserve dataset context beside the bytes A byte-count inventory detects missing or truncated content, but equal-length abc and abd expose its limit. The following Rust function demonstrates that narrow baseline; it does not reenact a historical dataset project’s full process. The course-local byte-count baseline accepts both three-byte inputs, abc and abd; it does not establish content identity or provenance. rust/demos/ch41-governed-corpus-acquisition/src/lib.rs#size-only-contrast pub fn size_only_accepts(expected_bytes: u64, supplied: &[u8]) -> bool { supplied.len() as u64 == expected_bytes } A byte inventory alone does not preserve a dataset’s collection context, provenance or suitability for language-model training. Datasheets for Datasets proposes structured dataset documentation; the later ROOTS corpus describes data creation, curation and governance for a multilingual language-model corpus. Datasheets for Datasets, first posted in 2018 and revised in the linked 2021 version, provides the earlier example. Gebru and colleagues propose dataset documentation describing motivation, composition, collection and recommended uses to improve communication, transparency and accountability. A checksum cannot replace those informed judgments. The BigScience ROOTS Corpus is described in a 2023 preprint. The ROOTS corpus paper documents data creation and curation with governance foregrounded in a multilingual language-model project; it does not validate this chapter’s fixture. The tiny manifest is not the ROOTS governance process or proof of corpus suitability. Keep selected corpus bytes linked to their source context before downstream filtering, split construction and training. Byte agreement does not establish quality, privacy or permission. Documentation records context; byte verification checks agreement with a selection. Neither alone establishes privacy, permission or training quality.
Read the evidence directly A spatial diagram would not clarify these record comparisons. The payload table states exactly which bytes belong to each role; the Rust report records identity changes, digest refusal and complete replay directly. Together they distinguish the selected corpus record, its supplied bytes and the synthetic scope of the example.
Optional practice: reproduce and explain the checks Run each command below from the repository root with Docker installed and running. Each selected check should report running 1 test and 1 passed; 0 failed; zero selected tests means the named check did not run. As with the demo, COURSE_CORPUS=false skips the optional corpus during image preparation; the supported wrapper runs the tests with network disabled. Reproduce the same-size corruption and explain why its length passes but its content is refused. COURSE_CORPUS=false ./course run cargo test --offline --locked \ -p ch41-governed-corpus-acquisition \ --test governed_acquisition \ size_digest_truncation_and_overrun_are_separate_failures -- --exact Reproduce the attribution-only variant. Identify which payload entry changes and which source references remain unchanged. COURSE_CORPUS=false ./course run cargo test --offline --locked \ -p ch41-governed-corpus-acquisition \ --test governed_acquisition \ provenance_changes_identity_without_changing_raw_digests -- --exact Reproduce verification and storage failures. Explain why a private candidate does not replace the last successfully published memory bundle. COURSE_CORPUS=false ./course run cargo test --offline --locked \ -p ch41-governed-corpus-acquisition \ --test governed_acquisition \ failure_preserves_prior_bundle_without_publishing_partial_candidate -- --exact Checked explanations for the three corpus-content verification tasks Both abc and abd contain 3 bytes, but their digests differ. The selected entry expects the digest of abc; the verifier returns Hash for abd instead of admitting it as the selected content. Only the attribution payload entry’s count and digest change. Both sources still refer to content ID attribution, and the raw text entries keep their original digests. The changed canonical manifest changes the identity. The variant needs its own independently selected policy. The test injects a corrupt final payload and separate write, finish and publication failures. In each case the memory store keeps the prior bundle and publishes no replacement. Earlier verified payloads remain in private staging, not in a partially admitted bundle. This is the tested memory-store boundary, not a guarantee of crash recovery for arbitrary storage.
What this supplies to the decoder pipeline The scalar reference remains unchanged. This boundary supplies selected, verified corpus content to later filtering and tokenization. The offline fixture is not acquired TinyStories or Chapter 42’s real input. Real input needs its own selected provenance and verified bytes; a fixture cannot be relabeled as training-data acquisition. Quality, privacy, contamination and final split selection remain separate questions.

<!DOCTYPE html><html lang="en" dir="ltr" data-diagram-full-view-open="View diagram full screen" data-diagram-full-view-close="Exit full screen" data-theme-storage-key="learn-llm-color-theme" data-astro-cid-z4jru4n3> <head><meta charset="UTF-8"><meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width"><meta name="description" content="Each localized chapter adds one tested idea to the same Rust implementation."><meta name="generator" content="Astro v7.1.1"><meta name="color-scheme" content="light dark"><script data-theme-bootstrap>
  (() => {
    const root = document.documentElement;
    const storageKey = root.dataset.themeStorageKey;
    if (!storageKey) return;

    let storedTheme = null;
    try {
      storedTheme = window.localStorage.getItem(storageKey);
    } catch {
      // Storage can be unavailable; the system preference remains usable.
    }

    if (storedTheme === 'light' || storedTheme === 'dark') {
      root.dataset.theme = storedTheme;
    } else {
      delete root.dataset.theme;
    }
  })();

<h2 id="the-problem-available-text-does-not-identify-a-training-corpus">The problem: available text does not identify a training corpus</h2>
<p>An LLM learns from the text supplied to its training pipeline. A filename alone
does not identify that text: two files named <code>train.txt</code> can contain different
bytes. A source can also change between revisions. Even the intended text is an
incomplete corpus record if its source revision, license text or attribution
has been lost.</p>
<p>Before filtering or tokenizing, we need to connect the selected text to its
documented origin and check that the supplied bytes match that selection. The
same check should work whether those bytes arrive from a file, an HTTP client
or another reader, and whether the verified bundle is kept in memory, files or
another store. How bytes travel and where they are kept do not change which
content was selected.</p>
<p>This chapter implements that content boundary. Verification does not clean the
text, establish privacy, grant legal permission or measure its usefulness for
training.</p>
<h2 id="start-with-a-complete-tiny-corpus-bundle">Start with a complete, tiny corpus bundle</h2>
<p>The example uses course-authored test bytes, not a downloaded training dataset.
A <strong>payload</strong> is one byte sequence included in the bundle. A <strong>content ID</strong> is
its logical name within the selected record, not a filename or a URL.</p>

<p>The fixture’s license identifier is <code>LicenseRef-Course-Test-Only</code>, and its
redistribution labels are <code>not-approved</code>. These describe the synthetic record,
not permission for a real corpus or a trained model. The held-out source is raw
input; its name does not define the final validation or test split.</p>

<h2 id="the-solution-select-the-record-then-verify-its-content">The solution: select the record, then verify its content</h2>
<p>A <strong>manifest</strong> records the bundle. Each payload entry supplies a content ID,
role, media type, exact byte count and SHA-256 digest. Each source record names
the corresponding content ID, source revision, provenance reference, license
and attribution. The provenance reference is descriptive evidence; it need not
be a URL and is not an instruction to fetch anything.</p>
<p>The caller must select the expected record independently of the candidate
being checked. Rust’s <code>DatasetPolicy</code> stores that selection. Copying an
untrusted candidate into the expected policy would check only its internal
consistency, not whether it was the intended corpus. The verifier cannot make
the caller’s provenance claims true merely by matching them.</p>
<p>For this tiny example, the selected record contains <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em"></span><span class="mord">2</span></span></span></span> sources and <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em"></span><span class="mord">4</span></span></span></span> payloads.
The reusable verifier does not require those counts. Other selections can name
different numbers of sources, share metadata or include additional payloads.</p>
<p>The manifest has one <strong>canonical</strong> representation: compact UTF-8 JSON, object
keys sorted by their UTF-8 bytes, payload entries sorted by the UTF-8 bytes of
their content IDs, source entries sorted by the UTF-8 bytes of their source IDs,
and exactly one final newline. An incoming manifest
with different formatting or ordering is rejected, not silently rewritten.
This fixes the exact bytes used for identity:</p>

<h2 id="what-the-identity-formula-means">What the identity formula means</h2>
<p>Here <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">c</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">a</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">n</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">o</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">n</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">i</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">c</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">a</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">l</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">_</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">a</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">n</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">i</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">f</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">e</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">t</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">_</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">b</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">y</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">t</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">e</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{canonical\_manifest\_bytes}</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:1.0044em;vertical-align:-0.31em"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mord mathrm">canonical_manifest_bytes</span></span></span></span></span> is the complete canonical record,
including payload digests and provenance. <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">SHA256</mi><mo>⁡</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\operatorname{SHA256}</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6833em"></span><span class="mop"><span class="mord mathrm">SHA256</span></span></span></span></span> maps those
bytes to a <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>256</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">256</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em"></span><span class="mord">256</span></span></span></span>-bit digest. <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">a</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">r</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">t</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">i</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">f</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">a</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">c</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">t</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">_</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">i</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">d</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{artifact\_id}</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:1.0044em;vertical-align:-0.31em"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mord mathrm">artifact_id</span></span></span></span></span> is that digest, displayed
as <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>64</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">64</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em"></span><span class="mord">64</span></span></span></span> hexadecimal characters. It identifies a record; it is not a signature
or a permission, privacy or quality certificate.</p>
<p>Payload bytes affect the identity through their recorded counts and digests.
The verifier must still read the actual payloads. Hashing a manifest does not
prove that its claimed content exists.</p>

<h2 id="verify-supplied-bytes-without-choosing-their-transport">Verify supplied bytes without choosing their transport</h2>
<p>The content verifier performs three checks in order:</p>
<ol>
<li>Validate the candidate manifest’s structure and require exact agreement with
the independently selected policy, including its provenance and producer
identifiers.</li>
<li>Require the provider’s logical inventory to match the selected payload IDs
exactly. A missing, extra or duplicate ID causes refusal before payloads are
opened or destination staging is created.</li>
<li>Read every selected payload through standard Rust I/O. Compare its observed
length and digest with its selected entry. Accept the bundle only after every
payload passes.</li>
</ol>
<p><code>AssetSource</code> supplies the logical inventory and a standard <code>Read</code> reader for
each selected payload. The provider decides how to obtain those bytes. Filesystem
path safety and HTTP response handling belong to the relevant adapter or library,
not to the content checks. A future provider can implement the same interface
without adding a new retrieval mode to the verifier.</p>
<p><code>verify_payload_into</code> uses standard I/O to stream into a writer while the
course code counts bytes and updates the digest. For a selected <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em"></span><span class="mord">3</span></span></span></span>-byte payload,
it observes at most <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em"></span><span class="mord">4</span></span></span></span> bytes: the fourth distinguishes a complete <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em"></span><span class="mord">3</span></span></span></span>-byte stream
from a longer stream with the same prefix. That excess byte is not written to
the destination. A short stream fails with <code>Size</code>; so does an overrun.
Equal-length content with the wrong digest fails with <code>Hash</code>. A reader or
writer failure is <code>Io</code>, not successful end of input.</p>

<p>SHA-256 and JSON syntax use supporting libraries. Course Rust owns record
consistency, canonical ordering, selected-policy agreement, logical inventory
and the comparisons that decide admission.</p>
<h3 id="keep-incomplete-content-out-of-the-published-bundle">Keep incomplete content out of the published bundle</h3>
<p><code>AssetStore</code> creates a private stage with standard <code>Write</code> writers.
A writer may contain an unverified prefix when verification fails. Such bytes
must remain unpublished; the caller must not treat them as an admitted payload.</p>
<p><code>acquire_bundle</code> verifies each payload, finishes it in the private stage,
and calls <code>publish</code> only after the entire bundle passes. The storage adapter
owns atomic publication, durability and cleanup. The content algorithm does not
assume a directory layout, reserved manifest filename or database protocol.</p>
<p>The example uses a memory store. Its failed replacement leaves the prior bundle
unchanged and publishes no partial candidate. This demonstrates the admission
order and this store’s behavior, not crash durability for every possible storage
backend. An adapter must publish a complete bundle or none of it; a storage error
after publication may leave a complete bundle visible and must not be described
as proof of rollback.</p>

<h3 id="two-changes-that-expose-the-boundary">Two changes that expose the boundary</h3>
<p>Replacing <code>b"abc"</code> with <code>b"abd"</code> preserves the training payload’s <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em"></span><span class="mord">3</span></span></span></span>-byte
length. A byte-count check accepts the replacement, but the full verifier returns
<code>Hash</code>. This identifies a content mismatch, not what either text would teach
an LLM.</p>
<p>For a separate deliberate selection, change attribution to
<code>b"course-authored fixture v2\n"</code>. Its payload entry now records <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>27</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">27</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em"></span><span class="mord">27</span></span></span></span> bytes and
a different digest. The source records still refer to the same logical
attribution ID; the raw text digests remain unchanged. The new complete payload
totals <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>49</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">49</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em"></span><span class="mord">49</span></span></span></span> bytes, and its canonical manifest has a different identity.
The original policy refuses this variant until the caller independently selects
the new record; changing supplied metadata does not authorize itself.</p>
<p><code>replay_bundle</code> reads a canonical manifest, checks the selected artifact
identity and verifies every currently supplied payload again. It has no
destination-writing interface. Matching an old identity alone would not detect
payload bytes changed afterward.</p>
<p>The executable prints a report with scope <code>synthetic-offline-fixture</code>,
including all payload counts and digests, the attribution comparison,
complete replay and the preserved prior bundle. These are checked toy results,
not acquisition of a training dataset.</p>

<h2 id="history-preserve-dataset-context-beside-the-bytes">History: preserve dataset context beside the bytes</h2>
<p>A byte-count inventory detects missing or truncated content, but equal-length
<code>abc</code> and <code>abd</code> expose its limit. The following Rust function demonstrates
that narrow baseline; it does not reenact a historical dataset project’s full
process.</p>
<figure class="rust-source" data-source-path="rust/demos/ch41-governed-corpus-acquisition/src/lib.rs" data-source-region="size-only-contrast" data-astro-cid-i3uagjh5> <figcaption data-astro-cid-i3uagjh5> <span data-astro-cid-i3uagjh5>The course-local byte-count baseline accepts both three-byte inputs, abc and abd; it does not establish content identity or provenance.</span> <code dir="ltr" data-astro-cid-i3uagjh5>rust/demos/ch41-governed-corpus-acquisition/src/lib.rs#size-only-contrast</code> </figcaption> <pre class="astro-code github-dark-high-contrast rust-source-code" style="background-color:#0a0c10;color:#f0f3f6; overflow-x: auto;" tabindex="0" aria-label="Rust source: the limited corpus byte-count baseline" dir="ltr" data-astro-cid-i3uagjh5 data-language="rust"><code><span class="line"><span style="color:#FF9492">pub</span><span style="color:#FF9492"> fn</span><span style="color:#DBB7FF"> size_only_accepts</span><span style="color:#F0F3F6">(expected_bytes</span><span style="color:#FF9492">:</span><span style="color:#FFB757"> u64</span><span style="color:#F0F3F6">, supplied</span><span style="color:#FF9492">:</span><span style="color:#FF9492"> &</span><span style="color:#F0F3F6">[</span><span style="color:#FFB757">u8</span><span style="color:#F0F3F6">]) </span><span style="color:#FF9492">-></span><span style="color:#FFB757"> bool</span><span style="color:#F0F3F6"> {</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#F0F3F6">    supplied</span><span style="color:#FF9492">.</span><span style="color:#DBB7FF">len</span><span style="color:#F0F3F6">() </span><span style="color:#FF9492">as</span><span style="color:#FFB757"> u64</span><span style="color:#FF9492"> ==</span><span style="color:#F0F3F6"> expected_bytes</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#F0F3F6">}</span></span></code></pre> </figure>
<p>A byte inventory alone does not preserve a dataset’s collection context,
provenance or suitability for language-model training.
Datasheets for Datasets proposes structured dataset documentation; the later
ROOTS corpus describes data creation, curation and governance for a multilingual
language-model corpus.</p>
<p><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/1803.09010v8">Datasheets for Datasets</a>, first posted in
<span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>2018</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2018</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em"></span><span class="mord">2018</span></span></span></span> and revised in the linked <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>2021</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2021</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em"></span><span class="mord">2021</span></span></span></span> version, provides the earlier example.
Gebru and colleagues propose dataset documentation describing motivation,
composition, collection and recommended uses to improve communication,
transparency and accountability. A checksum cannot replace those informed
judgments.</p>
<p><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.03915v1">The BigScience ROOTS Corpus</a> is described
in a <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>2023</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2023</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em"></span><span class="mord">2023</span></span></span></span> preprint. The ROOTS corpus paper documents data creation and curation
with governance foregrounded in a multilingual language-model project; it does
not validate this chapter’s fixture. The tiny manifest is not the ROOTS
governance process or proof of corpus suitability.</p>
<p>Keep selected corpus bytes linked to their source context before downstream
filtering, split construction and training. Byte agreement does not establish
quality, privacy or permission. Documentation records context; byte verification
checks agreement with a selection. Neither alone establishes privacy, permission
or training quality.</p>

<h2 id="read-the-evidence-directly">Read the evidence directly</h2>
<p>A spatial diagram would not clarify these record comparisons. The payload table
states exactly which bytes belong to each role; the Rust report records identity
changes, digest refusal and complete replay directly. Together they distinguish
the selected corpus record, its supplied bytes and the synthetic scope of the
example.</p>

<details><summary>Checked explanations for the three corpus-content verification tasks</summary><ol>
<li>Both <code>abc</code> and <code>abd</code> contain <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em"></span><span class="mord">3</span></span></span></span> bytes, but their digests differ.
The selected entry expects the digest of <code>abc</code>; the verifier returns
<code>Hash</code> for <code>abd</code> instead of admitting it as the selected content.</li>
<li>Only the attribution payload entry’s count and digest change. Both sources
still refer to content ID <code>attribution</code>, and the raw text entries keep
their original digests. The changed canonical manifest changes the identity.
The variant needs its own independently selected policy.</li>
<li>The test injects a corrupt final payload and separate write, finish and
publication failures. In each case the memory store keeps the prior bundle
and publishes no replacement. Earlier verified payloads remain in private
staging, not in a partially admitted bundle. This is the tested memory-store
boundary, not a guarantee of crash recovery for arbitrary storage.</li>
</ol></details>

relabeled as training-data acquisition. Quality, privacy, contamination and

<h2 id="the-problem-changes-need-a-fixed-comparison-point">The problem: changes need a fixed comparison point</h2>
<p>The previous chapter joined the tokenizer, decoder, training, evaluation,
checkpoint and generation code. Now the course will extend that system. If the
data, configuration and code change together, a changed result no longer tells
you which version you observed. You need a fixed reference that identifies its
inputs and states exactly what its checks establish.</p>
<p>This chapter keeps the small scalar decoder unchanged. It gives that reference
an input identity and a report whose claims stay attached to their evidence.
The identity identifies the fixed inputs. The checks establish which behavior
this execution reproduced. Neither establishes useful laptop-scale capability.</p>
<h3 id="what-the-reference-actually-does">What the reference actually does</h3>
<p>The fixture assigns <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>8</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">8</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em"></span><span class="mord">8</span></span></span></span> documents to training, <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em"></span><span class="mord">2</span></span></span></span> to validation and <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em"></span><span class="mord">2</span></span></span></span> to test.
The decoder has <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>1188</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1188</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em"></span><span class="mord">1188</span></span></span></span> learned scalar parameters and context capacity <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em"></span><span class="mord">4</span></span></span></span> tokens.
Its primary training schedule and separately executed replay each perform <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>32</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">32</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em"></span><span class="mord">32</span></span></span></span> updates
on full batches of <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>16</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">16</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em"></span><span class="mord">16</span></span></span></span> windows, with <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em"></span><span class="mord">4</span></span></span></span> valid targets per window. Therefore,
each schedule consumes</p>
<span class="katex-display"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="block"><semantics><mrow><mn>32</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mn>16</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>2048</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">32\cdot16\cdot4=2048</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em"></span><span class="mord">32</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.2222em"></span><span class="mbin">⋅</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.2222em"></span></span><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em"></span><span class="mord">16</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.2222em"></span><span class="mbin">⋅</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.2222em"></span></span><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em"></span><span class="mord">4</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.2778em"></span><span class="mrel">=</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.2778em"></span></span><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em"></span><span class="mord">2048</span></span></span></span></span>
<p>valid training targets. One pipeline invocation includes both schedules: <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>4096</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4096</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em"></span><span class="mord">4096</span></span></span></span>
targets altogether. These counts are derived from the frozen full-batch
schedule, not from a new runtime token counter. Evaluation targets and generated
tokens are separate quantities.</p>
<p>The report’s <code>independent_schedules</code> field counts two separately executed copies
of the same schedule from training seed <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>39</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">39</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em"></span><span class="mord">39</span></span></span></span>, not statistically independent
seed samples.</p>
<p>The replay agrees bit for bit with the primary training result in this
execution. The selected decoder and frozen bigram then score the same <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>1744</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1744</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em"></span><span class="mord">1744</span></span></span></span>
overlapping test-window target slots. Their mean negative log-likelihoods are
approximately <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>3.866087547</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3.866087547</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em"></span><span class="mord">3.866087547</span></span></span></span> and <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>3.981342714</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3.981342714</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em"></span><span class="mord">3.981342714</span></span></span></span> nats per slot, respectively.
This known comparison is a regression check: rerunning it can expose changes
in the checked behavior. It is not an independent estimate of generalization.</p>
<p>There are only <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>442</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">442</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em"></span><span class="mord">442</span></span></span></span> within-document transition occurrences in those test
documents. Overlapping windows repeat occurrences, so <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>1744</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1744</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em"></span><span class="mord">1744</span></span></span></span> is not a count
of distinct transitions. A separate policy would score each occurrence once,
using the longest available causal prefix capped at four tokens and only its
newest-position distribution. This run does not report numeric mean NLL or
perplexity under that policy.</p>
<p>The checkpoint round trip preserves its encoded bytes, model and optimizer
bits, and tokenizer. The restored decoder reproduces logits for the fixed
<code>At</code> probe, encoded as token IDs <code>[67,118]</code>. Cached and complete-prefix generation
agree on token IDs <code>[260,34,34]</code>: Cyrillic <code>т</code> followed by two spaces. Agreement
checks the two generation paths; those three tokens do not demonstrate useful
language quality.</p>

<h2 id="the-identitys-symbols-and-fixed-settings">The identity’s symbols and fixed settings</h2>
<p><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>R</mi><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">r</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">e</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">f</mi></mrow></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R_{\mathrm{ref}}</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.8333em;vertical-align:-0.15em"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right:0.0077em">R</span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t vlist-t2"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height:0.3361em"><span style="top:-2.55em;margin-left:-0.0077em;margin-right:0.05em"><span class="pstrut" style="height:2.7em"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mtight"><span class="mord mtight"><span class="mord mathrm mtight" style="margin-right:0.0778em">ref</span></span></span></span></span></span><span class="vlist-s">​</span></span><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height:0.15em"><span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span> is a <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>256</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">256</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em"></span><span class="mord">256</span></span></span></span>-bit digest, displayed as <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>64</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">64</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em"></span><span class="mord">64</span></span></span></span> lowercase hexadecimal
characters. Its three named inputs are:</p>
<ul>
<li><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">c</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">o</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">n</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">f</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">i</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi></mrow><mn>1188</mn></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{config}_{1188}</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.9386em;vertical-align:-0.2441em"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mord"><span class="mord mathrm" style="margin-right:0.0139em">config</span></span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t vlist-t2"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height:0.207em"><span style="top:-2.4559em;margin-right:0.05em"><span class="pstrut" style="height:2.7em"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mtight"><span class="mord mtight">1188</span></span></span></span></span><span class="vlist-s">​</span></span><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height:0.2441em"><span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span>: a canonical record of eighteen tiny-run settings,
together with the invariant that the decoder has <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>1188</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1188</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em"></span><span class="mord">1188</span></span></span></span> parameters.</li>
<li><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">f</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">i</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">x</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">t</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">u</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">r</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">e</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{fixture}</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6944em"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mord mathrm">fixture</span></span></span></span></span>: a canonical record of SHA-256 digests of the exact corpus
bytes and exact split-manifest bytes. Even a byte change that leaves parsed
JSON meaning unchanged creates a different input identity.</li>
<li><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">o</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">u</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">r</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">c</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">e</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">_</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">r</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">e</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">v</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">i</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">i</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">o</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">n</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{source\_revision}</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.9779em;vertical-align:-0.31em"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mord mathrm">source_revision</span></span></span></span></span>: a verified source identity combining a baseline
revision with the exact forty course-owned scalar-reference source files.</li>
</ul>
<p>Here <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">∥</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Vert</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:1em;vertical-align:-0.25em"></span><span class="mord">∥</span></span></span></span> means composition into the shared identity format’s named,
canonical fields, not writing three unframed strings beside one another.
That distinction matters: without field boundaries, different input sequences
can have the same concatenated bytes. The helper orders fields, serializes one
unambiguous record and hashes its complete bytes.</p>
<p>The settings fix eight BPE merges; decoder width, feed-forward width and context
capacity of four; one attention head and one block; stride one; training and
evaluation batch sizes of sixteen and one hundred twenty-eight; thirty-two
updates; learning rate <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>0.04</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.04</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em"></span><span class="mord">0.04</span></span></span></span>; gradient-norm cap <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em"></span><span class="mord">1</span></span></span></span>; training seed <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>39</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">39</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em"></span><span class="mord">39</span></span></span></span>;
generation seed <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>38</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">38</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em"></span><span class="mord">38</span></span></span></span>; bigram smoothing <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em"></span><span class="mord">1</span></span></span></span>; generation temperature <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>0.8</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.8</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em"></span><span class="mord">0.8</span></span></span></span>;
top-k four; and three generated tokens. The identity records floating-point
settings by their exact bit patterns rather than rounded display text.</p>

<p>The example verifies its compiled reference-source evidence first. It then
rejects changed corpus or split bytes before training or checkpoint work.
Only accepted fixed inputs reach the existing pipeline. The wrapper calls that
pipeline once; the pipeline itself performs primary training and replay.</p>

<h3 id="what-matching-identities-do-not-prove">What matching identities do not prove</h3>
<p>A matching digest identifies the same canonical input record, subject to the
hash’s collision-resistance assumption. It does not prove that the algorithm
is correct or that a new machine will reproduce every floating-point bit.</p>
<p>The source identity deliberately covers the forty scalar-reference source
files, not this chapter’s reporting wrapper or interface. Toolchain, locked
dependencies and arithmetic environment are recorded separately. A matching
source digest is therefore not evidence that two execution environments match.
The temporary checkpoint path is also outside the input identity; changing
that path does not change the model’s fixed inputs.</p>
<p>Likewise, exact checkpoint reload is narrower than complete job resumption.
This check does not restore every data cursor, in-flight operation or whole-job
continuation state. No laptop throughput is measured here.</p>

<h2 id="history-reporting-conditions-and-measuring-variation">History: reporting conditions and measuring variation</h2>
<p>A language-model score without its input conditions and scope does not identify
what was evaluated or establish which capabilities were checked.</p>
<p><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/1810.03993v2">Model Cards for Model Reporting</a> was
presented in 2019. Mitchell and colleagues propose model documentation that
includes intended uses and evaluation conditions; a model card is not itself
proof of quality.</p>
<p>Model Cards describe evaluation conditions and intended uses; later fine-tuning
experiments study variation across initializations and data orders. Reporting
scope and measuring variation answer different questions.</p>
<p>In <a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2002.06305v1">Fine-Tuning Pretrained Language Models: Weight Initializations, Data Orders, and Early Stopping</a>,
published in 2020, Dodge and colleagues study fine-tuning variability associated
with initialization and data order for pretrained language models. This does
not measure variability in the course’s tiny decoder.</p>
<p>Keep a fixed regression reference when changing an LLM pipeline, while recording
separately the evidence needed for quality, seed sensitivity and hardware claims.</p>
<p>The Rust reporting contrast uses the same observation. Reading only the mean
NLL with this expression gives a number:</p>
<pre class="astro-code github-dark-high-contrast" style="background-color:#0a0c10;color:#f0f3f6;overflow-x:auto" tabindex="0" data-language="rust" dir="ltr"><code><span class="line"><span style="color:#F0F3F6">trace</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#FF9492">    .</span><span style="color:#DBB7FF">observation</span><span style="color:#F0F3F6">()</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#FF9492">    .</span><span style="color:#DBB7FF">final_evaluation</span><span style="color:#F0F3F6">()</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#FF9492">    .</span><span style="color:#DBB7FF">decoder</span><span style="color:#F0F3F6">()</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#FF9492">    .</span><span style="color:#DBB7FF">mean_nll</span><span style="color:#F0F3F6">()</span></span></code></pre>
<p><code>trace.report()</code> also states the evaluation unit, input identity, replay
accounting and limits. It does not retrain a historical model or execute a seed
sweep.</p>

<p>Repeating seed <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>39</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">39</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em"></span><span class="mord">39</span></span></span></span> checks repeatability under fixed conditions. It does not
estimate variability across seeds. Those are complementary checks, not
interchangeable evidence.</p>

<h2 id="run-the-reference-without-changing-its-inputs">Run the reference without changing its inputs</h2>
<p>The example obtains verified source evidence and owns its temporary checkpoint
location. Its report comes directly from the checked scalar observation, not
from parsing a previous human-readable report.</p>

# Chapter 41 revision 5 evidence and commitments

Author evidence, not learner prose or a publication verdict. Package exact source,
tests, generated output and primary evidence separately. The edited contract is
a projection to verify, not independent proof of its own claims.

## Revision 5 scope and evidence provenance

This author adopts the C1–C8 semantic commitments below for the current candidate,
not the prior candidate's review verdicts. Only the four existing history
commitments are made explicit in their visible history paragraphs, and the
contract, lesson and English catalog revision changes from4to5. Topic, formula,
Rust, fixture, expected stdout, runnable commands, exercises, answers and glossary
remain unchanged. All four complete current English source documents and their
actual built presentation remain in the technical review's scope.

The preceding revision4 source baseline and commitment map are the exact
canonical-v4c artifacts, never the retired candidate02 English specification.
The baseline map SHA256 is
b7cb989d6069c88b22c3ee6b9dacfdc3f79a5223412e75f0df3d9b2e537bbe21.
Copying an old evidence file or role method is not a fresh execution or a judgment
of this candidate. Packaging must bind the actual current artifact-library source
bytes and accepted artifact-validation receipt. That4479byte receipt's SHA256 is
c3192bd578ef5575d54ec8cc4ce5d71cc8e0607483324bc0543f22e58af7b6fd;
its executed input manifest SHA256 is
9dfb78611182a9d80d49b7224b113d5ea95dc8599d952e69e162fc4642ca804d.
The machinery owner verified that each current artifact-source hash matches that
receipt. Reuse unchanged demo/fixture/test/golden evidence only after exact input
and provenance checks, never claim a new Rust run for this prose-only correction.

The author reopened the two approved arXiv primary records and inspected the
existing bounded history-sources.md observations. Their claims and date limits
still apply:2018is the first Datasheets posting,2021is the linked revision;
2023is the linked ROOTS preprint posting, not a denial of its NeurIPS2022record.
This is an author source observation, not retained raw HTTP response bytes,
an acquisition receipt or evidence of a third source.

The visible history must carry locally: the byte-inventory limitation; Datasheets
documentation followed by ROOTS multilingual creation/curation/governance; the
Datasheets motivation/composition/collection/recommended-use purposes; ROOTS's
bounded contribution and non-validation of the fixture; and source context before
filtering/splitting/training without a quality/privacy/permission certificate.
The course-local Rust byte-count comparison and all existing historical source
URLs, explicit dates and suitability limits stay intact. Metadata, paragraphs
and source-only isolated values must agree; proximity to another distant surface
does not replace a missing local referent or condition.

Use the actual canonical-v4c semantic grouping method only where the current
reading order or accessibility relationship still presents that group. The
author must inspect the concrete current extraction and every neutral requirement
before freeze. Freeze fresh source/HTML/context/settings and obtain four fresh
independent judgments; retain no old review as approval of revision5. Preserve
unchanged shared atoms as exact baseline invariants without claiming that this
candidate newly authors or approves unrelated copy. Russian41+ remains deferred;
there are no routine screenshots or image-approval gates.

## C1 — Problem, trust and scope

Evidence: DatasetPolicy::{new,from_config_bytes,validate_manifest}; test
selected_policy_is_independent_of_candidate_metadata; user-authorized complete
Chapter41 replacement without compatibility. A caller selects the expected
manifest independently of a candidate. Exact typed record agreement does not
authenticate the caller's selection or certify its provenance claims. A filename,
successful retrieval or a record's self-consistency does not identify the intended
training input. Teach content/provenance agreement, not acquisition transport,
privacy, rights, cleaning, training quality or final split selection. Preserve the
scalar decoder; the course-authored fixture is not acquired TinyStories. Metadata,
opening, policy explanation, glossary and handoff carry this bounded meaning.

## C2 — Literal inputs and separate byte quantities

Evidence: demo constants TRAIN, VALIDATION, LICENSE, ATTRIBUTION,
VARIANT_ATTRIBUTION; fixture source-policy.json; generated run_fixture report;
fixture_verifies_complete_content_not_real_corpus_approval. Derivation: abc has
3bytes, hello plusLF6, fixture-only plusLF13, attribution plusLF24. Two raw
sequences total9bytes; four payloads total46bytes, excluding the manifest.
Attribution variant27bytes yields49payloadbytes. One escaped newline is one byte.
Two source records share license/attribution content IDs, inventoried once.
Names train/validation are selected logical IDs, not storage paths or final split
proof. Table roles/headers, nearby explanation, worked_inputs and practice answers
preserve these units and mappings. Producer zeros and fixture-only rights labels
are synthetic, never real provenance/permission approval.

## C3 — Manifest structure and exact identity

Evidence: canonical_manifest::{validate_manifest_structure,canonical_manifest_bytes,
parse_dataset_manifest,artifact_id}; canonical_manifest_has_exact_bytes_and_no_legacy_decoder;
duplicate_unknown_and_unsorted_fields_are_refused. Closed v2 typed JSON, compact
UTF8, object keys in UTF8 byte order, payloads by contentID and sources by sourceID,
one finalLF. Exact reencoding equality rejects noncanonical input; no v1 decoder.
SHA256 supporting library hashes the complete canonical record, producing256bits
displayed as64hexcharacters. Payloads affect the record through counts/digests;
actual bytes must still be checked. No digest self-field, signature, authentication
or permission/quality assurance. Formula, symbols, canonical explanation and
identity caption/definition carry this distinction.

## C4 — Selected logical inventory and standard I/O

Evidence: inventory::{AssetSource,admit_inventory,verify_payload_into,verify_bundle};
missing_extra_duplicate_inventory_refuses_before_open_or_stage;
source_and_payload_counts_are_selected_not_hardcoded;
opaque_content_ids_are_not_paths_and_are_case_sensitive;
standard_read_supports_small_chunks_interruptions_and_trait_objects.
Order: validate candidate and independent policy, compare complete logical-ID
inventory, then open/read every selected payload. Source count/roles/media are
selected data, not hardcoded2/4/coreHTTP variants. ContentIDs are opaque exact
UTF8 labels, not paths; standard Read providers own retrieval and inventory truth.
Core counts/hashes; standard I/O owns streaming and I/O retry/error handling.
Files/HTTP/DB are extension roles, not a claim all adapters are implemented.
Provider inventory must be exact before stage/dataopen; all payloads must pass.
Length mismatches are Size, equal-length changed bytes Hash, I/O failures Io.
No transport response/redirect parsing is taught or implemented in these modules.

## C5 — EOF, bounds and provisional writes

Evidence: verify_payload_into; size_digest_truncation_and_overrun_are_separate_failures;
excess_byte_is_observed_but_not_written; empty_content_is_distinct_from_missing_content;
reader_and_flush_errors_are_not_successful_eof;
unrepresentable_eof_probe_is_refused_before_read.
Selected length3 permits reading at most4bytes; fourth byte detects overrun and
is not written. Standard Read EOF is observed, not inferred from merely reaching
expected count. Sink can contain an unverified prefix after failure; no arbitrary
writer rollback guarantee. Checked count arithmetic refuses overflow. SHA256 and
Serde are admitted supporting plumbing, not hidden content decisions. Rust
caption and length explanation retain actual write/failure scope.

## C6 — External storage admission and complete replay

Evidence: acquisition::{AssetStore,StagedAssets,acquire_bundle,replay_bundle}; demo
MemoryStore/MemoryStage/MemoryWriter; in_memory_destination_publishes_once_and_replay_checks_current_bytes;
failure_preserves_prior_bundle_without_publishing_partial_candidate;
replay_refuses_wrong_identity_and_noncanonical_record_before_payloads.
Core stages only after policy/inventory, verifies+finishes each private payload,
then requests one complete publication. Store owns atomic visibility, durability,
cleanup and concrete persistence format. Core specifies no directory/filename/DB.
Memory fixture proves priorbundle preserved on corrupt finalpayload and separate
write/finish/publication failures, not crash durability for all stores. A complete
entry can remain visible after a later durability error; never claim universal
rollback. Replay checks canonicalrecord, selectedidentity, policy/inventory and
all currentpayloads, with no destinationwrite interface. Store section, caption,
report/practice and answer preserve these conditions and bounded inferences.

## C7 — Independent content changes

Evidence: run_fixture, size_only_accepts;
provenance_changes_identity_without_changing_raw_digests.
abc→abd keeps3bytes but Hashrefuses under selectedabc digest. Attribution variant
changes only that payloadentry count/digest: logical source references and raw
digests remain unchanged. Manifest identity differs; original selectedpolicy
refuses the variant. Fixture explicitly selects a distinct policy for comparison;
candidate metadata never authorizes itself. No assumption of fixedsource counts.
This is a course-local comparison, not a claim about a historical project's code.

## C8 — History, sequence, practice and handoff

Primary evidence: Datasheets arXiv1803.09010v8 abstract (first2018, version2021):
motivation/composition/collection/recommendeduses, communication/transparency/
accountability. ROOTS arXiv2303.03915v1 abstract (2023): multilingual data creation,
curation and governance. Neither describes this Rust manifest or certifies fixture.
Course-local sequence: problem→explained solution/formula/Rust→history→direct
record evidence→optional reproduction. No prediction questions. Table/report are
more informative than spatial diagram for these byte/record comparisons. Nofigure.
Every run task has exact repo-root COURSE_CORPUS=false ./course run command,
Docker prerequisite, truthful image-build network/dependency context and
nonzero selectedtest result. Three named practice cases and checked explanations
match actualtests. Englishonly currentrollout; noRussianstub. Scalarunchanged;
Chapter42 needs separately acquired/verified realinput, not relabeled fixture.

## Affected surfaces and author requirements

Complete lesson/HTML: explain the need for selected provenance, independent-policy
trust boundary, exact canonical identity, logical inventory, standard I/O checks,
external store admission and current-byte replay using actual synthetic evidence;
keep quantities/conditions/failures local, history bounded, practice optional and
handoff distinct from real acquisition/privacy/rights/quality/final splits.

Complete contract: correctly project C1–C8 into learner fields and exact observed
output; keep internal implementation/delivery instructions separate from teaching.
Complete catalog: identify this English corpus-provenance/content-verification
chapter and destination, not a transport-protocol lesson or real-corpus claim.
Complete sheet: six concise chapter-used terms with local referents and limits.
Course index/neighbor navigation: accurate existing English destination and topic,
preserving predecessor teaching and not claiming Russian41 availability.

Reading units follow actual H2 section boundaries, preserving nested H3/Rust,
tables, commands and answers in their presented order. Freeze each section's
requirement against the C1–C8 operations it contains. Contextual headings orient
within those sections; do not treat headings as standalone catalog descriptions.
Standalone metadata/catalog descriptions must name corpus/content/provenance
scope without nearbyprose. Captions/accessiblenames identify the particular Rust
operation, corpus object and measured/synthetic boundary they label. Table headers
name ID/role/literal/countcolumn and countunit. Term+definition form each actual
glossaryunit. Commands and their local task form the presented practiceunit.
Shared unchanged controls retain their actual glossary/navigation accessibility
roles and neutral requirements, not inherited candidate publication verdicts.

Return deterministic extracted surface proposal for author to assign/check each
exact frozen role requirement before routing. Packaging does not judge pedagogy,
requirements, technical truth or language quality.

## Initial concrete surface bindings

All commitments affect source.contract, source.lesson and built.lesson. Additional
newly inventoried source-only/grouped units are bound by the final author role map.

- C1: source.catalog, source.sheet, reading.001, reading.003, reading.009,
  unit.001, unit.011, unit.017, unit.021, unit.022, unit.028, unit.051.
- C2: source.sheet, reading.002, unit.018, unit.020, unit.023, unit.024,
  unit.025, unit.026, unit.027.
