#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

repository_root=$(CDPATH= cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
workspace_image=learn-llm-workspace:local
site_image=learn-llm-site:local
tools_image=learn-llm-agent-tools:local
tools_directory="$repository_root/tools"
tools_base_digest=sha256:5b8f294aff9041b7191c34a4bab3ac270157a28774d4b0660e9743297b697e48
tools_snapshot_id=20260811T091000Z

fail() {
  printf 'error: %s\n' "$*" >&2
  exit 2
}

course_corpus_mode=${COURSE_CORPUS:-true}
case $course_corpus_mode in
  true|false) ;;
  *) fail 'COURSE_CORPUS must be true or false' ;;
esac

usage() {
  cat <<'EOF'
Usage: ./course COMMAND [ARGUMENTS]

Commands:
  build                         Build the deployable static-site image.
  release                       Atomically export that image to site/dist.
  review RUN_ID [PORT]          Render and serve a staged run on loopback.
  review RUN_ID --port PORT     Choose a loopback port (default: 4321).
  review RUN_ID --check         Build and verify the staged site without serving.
  run COMMAND [ARGUMENTS]       Run one command in the workspace image.
  check                         Build the validated workspace image.
  preview                       Serve the canonical deployable image on port 4321.
  smoke                         Check the canonical preview at 127.0.0.1:4321.
  audit-host                    Reject host toolchain/dependency/cache artifacts.
  tools build                   Build the pinned offline agent-tools image (networked).
  tools test                    Run agent-tools tests offline in the pinned image.
  tools verify-run RUN_ID --manifest RELPATH
                                Verify one run manifest offline.
  tools visual-evidence RUN_ID --contract RELPATH
                                Generate visual evidence offline.
  help                          Show this help.
EOF
}

build_workspace_image() {
  docker build --target workspace -t "$workspace_image" --build-arg "COURSE_CORPUS=$course_corpus_mode" "$repository_root"
}

build_site_image() {
  docker build --target site -t "$site_image" --build-arg "COURSE_CORPUS=$course_corpus_mode" "$repository_root"
}

tools_source_hash() {
  local path
  local -a source_paths=(
    "Dockerfile"
    "luna/verify-run.mjs"
    "terra/visual-evidence.mjs"
    "tests/docker"
    "tests/verify-run.test.mjs"
    "tests/visual-evidence.test.mjs"
  )

  [[ -d $tools_directory && ! -L $tools_directory ]] ||
    fail "agent-tools source directory is missing or unsafe: $tools_directory"
  for path in "${source_paths[@]}"; do
    [[ -f "$tools_directory/$path" && ! -L "$tools_directory/$path" ]] ||
      fail "agent-tools source is missing or unsafe: $tools_directory/$path"
  done
  (
    cd -- "$tools_directory"
    sha256sum -- "${source_paths[@]}" | sha256sum | awk '{print $1}'
  )
}

tools_lock_hash() {
  local lock="$tools_directory/toolchain.lock.json"
  [[ -f $lock && ! -L $lock ]] || fail "agent-tools lock is missing or unsafe: $lock"
  sha256sum -- "$lock" | awk '{print $1}'
}

build_tools_image() {
  local lock_hash source_hash
  lock_hash=$(tools_lock_hash)
  source_hash=$(tools_source_hash)
  docker build --pull \
    --file "$tools_directory/Dockerfile" \
    --tag "$tools_image" \
    --build-arg "TOOLCHAIN_LOCK_SHA256=$lock_hash" \
    --build-arg "TOOLS_SOURCE_SHA256=$source_hash" \
    "$tools_directory"
}

validate_tools_image() {
  local lock_hash source_hash image_lock_hash image_source_hash image_base_digest
  local image_snapshot image_platform
  docker image inspect --format '{{.Id}}' "$tools_image" >/dev/null 2>&1 ||
    fail "agent-tools image is not available; run './course tools build' first"
  lock_hash=$(tools_lock_hash)
  source_hash=$(tools_source_hash)
  image_lock_hash=$(docker image inspect --format \
    '{{index .Config.Labels "org.learn-llm.toolchain-lock-sha256"}}' "$tools_image") ||
    fail "cannot inspect agent-tools lock attestation"
  image_source_hash=$(docker image inspect --format \
    '{{index .Config.Labels "org.learn-llm.tools-source-sha256"}}' "$tools_image") ||
    fail "cannot inspect agent-tools source attestation"
  image_base_digest=$(docker image inspect --format \
    '{{index .Config.Labels "org.opencontainers.image.base.digest"}}' "$tools_image") ||
    fail "cannot inspect agent-tools base-image attestation"
  image_snapshot=$(docker image inspect --format \
    '{{index .Config.Labels "org.learn-llm.ubuntu.snapshot"}}' "$tools_image") ||
    fail "cannot inspect agent-tools Ubuntu-snapshot attestation"
  image_platform=$(docker image inspect --format '{{.Os}}/{{.Architecture}}' "$tools_image") ||
    fail "cannot inspect agent-tools platform"
  [[ $image_lock_hash == "$lock_hash" ]] ||
    fail "agent-tools image lock attestation is stale (image=$image_lock_hash current=$lock_hash)"
  [[ $image_source_hash == "$source_hash" ]] ||
    fail "agent-tools image source attestation is stale (image=$image_source_hash current=$source_hash)"
  [[ $image_base_digest == "$tools_base_digest" ]] ||
    fail "agent-tools image base digest is unexpected: $image_base_digest"
  [[ $image_snapshot == "$tools_snapshot_id" ]] ||
    fail "agent-tools image snapshot is unexpected: $image_snapshot"
  [[ $image_platform == linux/amd64 ]] ||
    fail "agent-tools image platform is unexpected: $image_platform"
}

validate_tools_relative_path() {
  local relative=$1 component
  [[ -n $relative ]] || fail 'tooling paths must not be empty'
  [[ $relative != /* && $relative != *\\* && $relative != *'//'* ]] ||
    fail "tooling path must be relative and normalized: $relative"
  [[ $relative =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9._/-]+$ ]] ||
    fail "tooling path contains unsafe characters: $relative"
  IFS=/ read -r -a path_components <<< "$relative"
  for component in "${path_components[@]}"; do
    [[ -n $component && $component != . && $component != .. ]] ||
      fail "tooling path contains an unsafe component: $relative"
  done
}

validate_tools_run() {
  local run_id=$1 relative=$2 run_directory target canonical_run canonical_target
  validate_run_id "$run_id"
  validate_tools_relative_path "$relative"
  run_directory="$repository_root/.build/runs/$run_id"
  [[ -d $run_directory && ! -L $run_directory ]] || fail "unknown or unsafe run: $run_id"
  target="$run_directory/$relative"
  [[ -f $target && ! -L $target ]] || fail "tooling input is missing or unsafe: $target"
  canonical_run=$(realpath -e -- "$run_directory")
  canonical_target=$(realpath -e -- "$target")
  [[ $canonical_target == "$canonical_run/"* ]] ||
    fail "tooling input escapes its run directory: $relative"
}

tools_runtime_mounts() {
  local output_directory=$1
  printf '%s\n' \
    "--mount" "type=bind,src=$repository_root,dst=/workspace,readonly" \
    "--mount" "type=bind,src=$output_directory,dst=/output"
}

prepare_tools_output() {
  local run_id=$1 output_name=$2
  local run_directory="$repository_root/.build/runs/$run_id"
  local tooling_directory="$run_directory/tooling"
  local output_directory="$tooling_directory/$output_name"
  local canonical_run canonical_output mode

  validate_run_id "$run_id"
  case "$output_name" in
    verify-run|visual-evidence) ;;
    *) fail "invalid tooling output name: $output_name" ;;
  esac
  [[ -d $run_directory && ! -L $run_directory ]] || fail "unknown or unsafe run: $run_id"
  canonical_run=$(realpath -e -- "$run_directory")

  if [[ -e $tooling_directory || -L $tooling_directory ]]; then
    [[ -d $tooling_directory && ! -L $tooling_directory ]] ||
      fail "tooling output parent is not a directory: $tooling_directory"
    mode=$(stat -c '%a' -- "$tooling_directory")
    [[ $mode == 700 ]] || fail "tooling output parent must be mode 0700: $tooling_directory"
  else
    (umask 077 && mkdir -- "$tooling_directory") ||
      fail "cannot create tooling output parent: $tooling_directory"
  fi

  [[ ! -e $output_directory && ! -L $output_directory ]] ||
    fail "refusing to reuse tooling output directory; failed evidence is preserved: $output_directory"
  (umask 077 && mkdir -- "$output_directory") ||
    fail "cannot create tooling output directory: $output_directory"
  mode=$(stat -c '%a' -- "$output_directory")
  [[ $mode == 700 ]] || fail "tooling output must be mode 0700: $output_directory"
  canonical_output=$(realpath -e -- "$output_directory")
  [[ $canonical_output == "$canonical_run/tooling/"* ]] ||
    fail "tooling output escapes its run directory: $output_name"
  printf '%s\n' "$canonical_output"
}

run_tools_container() {
  local run_id=$1 script=$2 relative_flag=$3 relative=$4 output_name=$5
  local container_input="/workspace/.build/runs/$run_id/$relative"
  local output_directory host_uid host_gid
  local -a mounts
  validate_tools_image
  output_directory=$(prepare_tools_output "$run_id" "$output_name")
  host_uid=$(id -u)
  host_gid=$(id -g)
  mapfile -t mounts < <(tools_runtime_mounts "$output_directory")
  docker run --pull=never --rm --network none --read-only \
    --tmpfs /tmp:rw,nosuid,nodev,noexec,size=536870912 \
    --cap-drop=ALL --security-opt no-new-privileges \
    --user "$host_uid:$host_gid" \
    --env LC_ALL=C --env TZ=UTC --env MAGICK_THREAD_LIMIT=1 \
    --env SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH=0 \
    "${mounts[@]}" --workdir /workspace \
    "$tools_image" /usr/bin/node "/opt/learn-llm-agent-tools/$script" \
    "$run_id" "$relative_flag" "$container_input" --output /output
}

run_tools_tests() {
  local host_uid host_gid
  validate_tools_image
  host_uid=$(id -u)
  host_gid=$(id -g)
  docker run --pull=never --rm --network none --read-only \
    --tmpfs /tmp:rw,nosuid,nodev,noexec,size=536870912 \
    --cap-drop=ALL --security-opt no-new-privileges \
    --user "$host_uid:$host_gid" \
    --env LC_ALL=C --env TZ=UTC --env MAGICK_THREAD_LIMIT=1 \
    --env SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH=0 --env CI_AGENT_TOOLS=1 \
    --env COURSE_SOURCE=/workspace/course \
    --mount "type=bind,src=$repository_root,dst=/workspace,readonly" \
    --workdir /workspace "$tools_image" /usr/bin/node --test \
    /opt/learn-llm-agent-tools/tests/verify-run.test.mjs \
    /opt/learn-llm-agent-tools/tests/visual-evidence.test.mjs
}

tools_command() {
  (($# > 0)) || fail 'tools requires a command'
  local subcommand=$1
  shift
  case "$subcommand" in
    build)
      (($# == 0)) || fail 'tools build takes no arguments'
      build_tools_image
      ;;
    test)
      (($# == 0)) || fail 'tools test takes no arguments'
      run_tools_tests
      ;;
    verify-run|visual-evidence)
      (($# >= 3)) || fail "tools $subcommand requires RUN_ID and one path option"
      local run_id=$1 option=$2 relative=$3
      shift 3
      (($# == 0)) || fail "tools $subcommand takes no extra arguments"
      if [[ $subcommand == verify-run ]]; then
        [[ $option == --manifest ]] || fail 'verify-run requires --manifest RELPATH'
        validate_tools_run "$run_id" "$relative"
        run_tools_container "$run_id" luna/verify-run.mjs --manifest "$relative" verify-run
      else
        [[ $option == --contract ]] || fail 'visual-evidence requires --contract RELPATH'
        validate_tools_run "$run_id" "$relative"
        run_tools_container "$run_id" terra/visual-evidence.mjs --contract "$relative" visual-evidence
      fi
      ;;
    *) fail "unknown tools command: $subcommand" ;;
  esac
}

cleanup_release() {
  local status=$?

  if [[ -n ${release_container_name:-} ]]; then
    docker rm -f "$release_container_name" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  fi

  if [[ -n ${release_temporary:-} ]]; then
    case "$release_temporary" in
      "$repository_root"/site/.release-*) rm -rf -- "$release_temporary" ;;
    esac
  fi

  if [[ -n ${release_lock_directory:-} ]]; then
    rmdir "$release_lock_directory" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  fi

  return "$status"
}

cleanup_review() {
  local status=$?

  if [[ -n ${review_logs_pid:-} ]]; then
    kill "$review_logs_pid" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
    wait "$review_logs_pid" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  fi

  if [[ -n ${review_container_name:-} ]]; then
    docker rm -f "$review_container_name" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  fi

  return "$status"
}

release_site() {
  local export_directory mv_help

  release_lock_directory="$repository_root/site/.release.lock"
  release_temporary=
  release_container_name=
  trap cleanup_release EXIT
  trap 'exit 130' INT
  trap 'exit 143' TERM
  mkdir "$release_lock_directory" 2>/dev/null || {
    release_lock_directory=
    fail "another release is running, or a stale lock exists: $repository_root/site/.release.lock"
  }

  mv_help=$(mv --help 2>&1)
  [[ $mv_help == *'--exchange'* && $mv_help == *'--no-copy'* ]] ||
    fail 'release requires GNU mv with --exchange and --no-copy support'
  build_site_image
  release_temporary=$(mktemp -d "$repository_root/site/.release-XXXXXXXX")
  export_directory="$release_temporary/export"
  mkdir -p "$export_directory"
  release_container_name="learn-llm-release-${release_temporary##*/}"
  docker create --name "$release_container_name" "$site_image" >/dev/null

  docker cp "$release_container_name:/usr/share/nginx/html/." "$export_directory"
  docker rm "$release_container_name" >/dev/null
  release_container_name=

  [[ -f "$export_directory/index.html" ]] || fail 'the site image has no root index.html'
  [[ -f "$export_directory/en/course/index.html" ]] || fail 'the site image has no English course index'
  [[ -f "$export_directory/ru/course/index.html" ]] || fail 'the site image has no Russian course index'

  if [[ -e "$repository_root/site/dist" ]]; then
    mv --exchange --no-copy -T "$export_directory" "$repository_root/site/dist"
    rm -rf -- "$export_directory"
  else
    mv --no-copy -T "$export_directory" "$repository_root/site/dist"
  fi

  rmdir "$release_temporary"
  release_temporary=
  rmdir "$release_lock_directory"
  release_lock_directory=
  trap - EXIT INT TERM

  printf 'Static release written atomically to %s\n' "$repository_root/site/dist"
}

validate_run_id() {
  local run_id=$1
  [[ ${#run_id} -le 128 ]] || fail 'run ID is too long'
  [[ $run_id =~ ^[0-9]{8}T[0-9]{6}Z-[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*-[0-9]{2}$ ]] ||
    fail 'run ID must match YYYYMMDDTHHMMSSZ-lowercase-step-name-NN'
}

validate_port() {
  local port=$1
  [[ $port =~ ^[1-9][0-9]*$ ]] || fail 'port must be a canonical positive integer'
  ((port >= 1024 && port <= 65535)) || fail 'port must be between 1024 and 65535'
}

verify_staged_manifest() {
  local run_directory=$1
  local publish_directory="$run_directory/publish"
  local manifest="$run_directory/publish.sha256"
  local unsafe_entry manifest_prefix line expected_hash staged_path
  local actual_hash hash_output repository_relative_path
  local manifest_count=0
  local staged_count=0
  declare -A expected_hashes=()

  unsafe_entry=$(find "$publish_directory" -mindepth 1 ! -type d ! -type f -print -quit)
  [[ -z $unsafe_entry ]] || fail "staged trees may contain only regular files and directories: $unsafe_entry"

  if [[ -L $manifest || ( -e $manifest && ! -f $manifest ) ]]; then
    fail "staged manifest must be a regular non-symlink file: $manifest"
  fi
  [[ -f $manifest ]] || return 0

  manifest_prefix=${publish_directory#"$repository_root/"}/
  while IFS= read -r line || [[ -n $line ]]; do
    [[ $line =~ ^([[:xdigit:]]{64})[[:space:]][[:space:]](.+)$ ]] ||
      fail "invalid staged manifest line: $line"
    expected_hash=${BASH_REMATCH[1],,}
    staged_path=${BASH_REMATCH[2]}
    [[ $staged_path == "$manifest_prefix"* ]] ||
      fail "staged manifest path escapes publish/: $staged_path"
    [[ -z ${expected_hashes[$staged_path]+present} ]] ||
      fail "duplicate staged manifest path: $staged_path"
    expected_hashes[$staged_path]=$expected_hash
    ((manifest_count += 1))
  done < "$manifest"

  while IFS= read -r -d '' staged_path; do
    repository_relative_path=${staged_path#"$repository_root/"}
    [[ -n ${expected_hashes[$repository_relative_path]+present} ]] ||
      fail "unlisted staged file: $repository_relative_path"
    hash_output=$(sha256sum -- "$staged_path")
    hash_output=${hash_output#\\}
    actual_hash=${hash_output%%[[:space:]]*}
    [[ $actual_hash == "${expected_hashes[$repository_relative_path]}" ]] ||
      fail "staged checksum mismatch: $repository_relative_path"
    unset 'expected_hashes[$repository_relative_path]'
    ((staged_count += 1))
  done < <(find "$publish_directory" -type f -print0 | sort -z)

  ((manifest_count == staged_count)) ||
    fail "staged manifest lists files that are missing or outside publish/"
}

discover_review_routes() {
  local publish_directory=$1
  local lesson_root="$publish_directory/site/src/content/chapters"
  local lesson relative locale filename slug

  review_routes=()
  review_files=()
  [[ -d $lesson_root ]] || return 0

  while IFS= read -r lesson; do
    relative=${lesson#"$lesson_root/"}
    locale=${relative%%/*}
    filename=${relative#*/}
    slug=${filename%.mdx}
    [[ $locale =~ ^[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+)*$ ]] || fail "unsafe staged locale path: $locale"
    [[ $slug =~ ^[0-9]{2}-[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+)*$ ]] || fail "unsafe staged chapter path: $slug"
    review_routes+=("/$locale/course/$slug/")
    review_files+=("/usr/share/nginx/html/$locale/course/$slug/index.html")
  done < <(find "$lesson_root" -mindepth 2 -maxdepth 2 -type f -name '*.mdx' -print | sort)
}

verify_review_image() {
  local review_image=$1
  local check_script='set -eu; test -f /usr/share/nginx/html/index.html'
  local route_file

  for route_file in "${review_files[@]}"; do
    check_script+="; test -f $route_file"
  done
  docker run --rm --entrypoint /bin/sh "$review_image" -c "$check_script"
}

review_run() {
  (($# >= 1)) || fail 'review requires a run ID'

  local run_id=$1
  local port=4321
  local check_only=false
  local port_was_set=false
  local run_directory publish_directory review_image argument route
  shift

  validate_run_id "$run_id"
  while (($# > 0)); do
    argument=$1
    shift
    case "$argument" in
      --check)
        $check_only && fail '--check was supplied more than once'
        check_only=true
        ;;
      --port)
        (($# > 0)) || fail '--port requires a value'
        $port_was_set && fail 'review port was supplied more than once'
        port=$1
        port_was_set=true
        shift
        ;;
      [0-9]*)
        $port_was_set && fail 'review port was supplied more than once'
        port=$argument
        port_was_set=true
        ;;
      *) fail "unknown review argument: $argument" ;;
    esac
  done
  validate_port "$port"

  run_directory="$repository_root/.build/runs/$run_id"
  publish_directory="$run_directory/publish"
  [[ -d $run_directory && ! -L $run_directory ]] || fail "unknown or unsafe run: $run_id"
  [[ -d $publish_directory && ! -L $publish_directory ]] || fail "run has no safe publish directory: $run_id"
  [[ -n $(find "$publish_directory" -mindepth 1 -print -quit) ]] || fail "run publish directory is empty: $run_id"

  verify_staged_manifest "$run_directory"
  discover_review_routes "$publish_directory"
  review_image="learn-llm-review:${run_id,,}"

  docker build \
    --build-context "staged=$publish_directory" \
    --build-arg "COURSE_CORPUS=$course_corpus_mode" \
    --target review-site \
    -t "$review_image" \
    "$repository_root"
  verify_review_image "$review_image"
  verify_staged_manifest "$run_directory"

  printf 'Rendered staged run %s without changing its publish tree.\n' "$run_id"
  if ((${#review_routes[@]} == 0)); then
    printf '  http://127.0.0.1:%s/\n' "$port"
  else
    for route in "${review_routes[@]}"; do
      printf '  http://127.0.0.1:%s%s\n' "$port" "$route"
    done
  fi

  $check_only && return 0

  printf 'Press Ctrl+C to stop the review server.\n'
  review_container_name="learn-llm-review-${run_id,,}-$$"
  review_logs_pid=
  trap cleanup_review EXIT
  trap 'exit 130' INT
  trap 'exit 143' TERM
  docker run --rm --init -d --name "$review_container_name" \
    -p "127.0.0.1:$port:80" "$review_image" >/dev/null
  docker logs --follow "$review_container_name" &
  review_logs_pid=$!
  wait "$review_logs_pid"
  review_logs_pid=
  review_container_name=
  trap - EXIT INT TERM
}

command=${1:-help}
case "$command" in
  build)
    (($# == 1)) || fail 'build takes no arguments'
    build_site_image

esac

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Offline execution plumbing only; the owning step authorizes the Cargo argv.
set -euo pipefail

fail() { printf 'error: %s\n' "$1" >&2; exit 2; }
[[ $# -ge 6 ]] || fail 'usage: run-functional-rust-overlay.sh RUN_ID OPERATION IMAGE_SHA -- cargo SUBCOMMAND ...'
run_id=$1
operation=$2
image=$3
[[ $run_id =~ ^[0-9]{8}T[0-9]{6}Z-[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+)*$ ]] || fail 'invalid run ID'
[[ $operation =~ ^[a-z][a-z0-9]*(-[a-z0-9]+)*$ ]] || fail 'invalid operation'
[[ $image =~ ^sha256:[0-9a-f]{64}$ ]] || fail 'exact cached image digest required'
[[ $4 == -- && $5 == cargo ]] || fail 'only a Cargo argv vector is accepted'
shift 4
case $2 in
  build|check|clippy|test|run|tree) [[ " $* " == *' --locked '* ]] || fail 'locked Cargo inputs required' ;;
  fmt) ;;
  *) fail 'unsupported Cargo subcommand; provisioning and arbitrary executables are excluded' ;;
esac

repository_root=$(pwd -P)
[[ -f $repository_root/Cargo.toml && -d $repository_root/rust && -d $repository_root/configs ]] || fail 'invoke from repository root'
run="$repository_root/.build/runs/$run_id"
[[ -d $run && $(realpath -e -- "$run") == "$run" ]] || fail 'existing nonsymlink run required'
[[ -d $run/publish && ! -L $run/publish ]] || fail 'regular publish stage required'
[[ -d $run/cargo-cache/registry && ! -L $run/cargo-cache ]] || fail 'provisioned run cache required'
deletion_mount=()
if [[ -e $run/deleted-files.json || -L $run/deleted-files.json ]]; then
  [[ -f $run/deleted-files.json && ! -L $run/deleted-files.json ]] || fail 'regular run-owned deletion manifest required'
  deletion_mount=(--mount "type=bind,source=$run/deleted-files.json,target=/deletions.json,readonly")
fi
[[ ! -L $run/validation && ! -L $run/rust-target && ! -L $run/.rust-overlay.lock ]] || fail 'unsafe output path'
mkdir -p -- "$run/validation" "$run/rust-target"
exec 9>"$run/.rust-overlay.lock"
flock -n 9 || fail 'another Rust overlay owns this run'
evidence="$run/validation/$operation"
[[ ! -e $evidence && ! -L $evidence ]] || fail 'operation evidence already exists; choose a fresh operation'
mkdir -m 0700 -- "$evidence"
printf '%s\n' "$image" > "$evidence/image.txt"
printf '%s\0' "$@" > "$evidence/argv.nul"

set +e
docker run --rm --pull never --network none \
  "${deletion_mount[@]}" \
  --tmpfs /work:rw,nosuid,nodev,size=512m,mode=0755 \
  -v "$repository_root:/repo:ro" -v "$run/publish:/staged:ro" \
  -v "$run/cargo-cache:/cache" -v "$run/rust-target:/target" \
  -v "$evidence:/evidence" \
  -e CARGO_HOME=/cache -e CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/target \
  -e "OVERLAY_OWNER_UID=$(id -u)" -e "OVERLAY_OWNER_GID=$(id -g)" \
  --entrypoint sh "$image" -c '
set -eu
test -z "$(find /staged -type l -print -quit)" || { echo "symlink in stage" >&2; exit 2; }
tar -C /repo -cf - Cargo.toml Cargo.lock rust configs | tar -C /work -xf -
cd /staged
find . -type f -print0 | tar --null -T - -cf - | tar -C /work -xf -
if [ -f /deletions.json ]; then
  node /repo/scripts/lib/functional-staging-deletions.mjs /deletions.json /work
fi
cd /work
find Cargo.toml Cargo.lock rust configs -type f -print0 | sort -z | xargs -0 sha256sum > /evidence/input-hashes.txt
if "$@" > /evidence/stdout.txt 2> /evidence/stderr.txt; then outcome=0; else outcome=$?; fi
printf "%s\n" "$outcome" > /evidence/cargo-exit-status.txt
chown -R "$OVERLAY_OWNER_UID:$OVERLAY_OWNER_GID" /evidence /target
cat /evidence/stdout.txt /evidence/stderr.txt
exit "$outcome"
' sh "$@" > "$evidence/launcher.stdout.txt" 2> "$evidence/launcher.stderr.txt"
outcome=$?
set -e
printf '%s\n' "$outcome" > "$evidence/launcher-exit-status.txt"
cat "$evidence/launcher.stdout.txt" "$evidence/launcher.stderr.txt"
exit "$outcome"

Each payload entry supplies a content ID, role, media type, exact byte count and SHA-256 digest. Each source record names the corresponding content ID, source revision, provenance reference, license and attribution. The provenance reference is descriptive evidence; it need not be a URL and is not an instruction to fetch anything. The caller must select the expected record independently of the candidate being checked. Rust’s DatasetPolicy stores that selection. Copying an untrusted candidate into the expected policy would check only its internal consistency, not whether it was the intended corpus. The verifier cannot make the caller’s provenance claims true merely by matching them. For this tiny example, the selected record contains 2 sources and 4 payloads. The reusable verifier does not require those counts. Other selections can name different numbers of sources, share metadata or include additional payloads. The manifest has one canonical representation: compact UTF-8 JSON, object keys sorted by their UTF-8 bytes, payload entries sorted by the UTF-8 bytes of their content IDs, source entries sorted by the UTF-8 bytes of their source IDs, and exactly one final newline. An incoming manifest with different formatting or ordering is rejected, not silently rewritten. supplied bytes without choosing their transport The content verifier performs three checks in order: Validate the candidate manifest’s structure and require exact agreement with the independently selected policy, including its provenance and producer identifiers. Require the provider’s logical inventory to match the selected payload IDs exactly. A missing, extra or duplicate ID causes refusal before payloads are opened or destination staging is created. Read every selected payload through standard Rust I/O. Compare its observed length and digest with its selected entry. Accept the bundle only after every payload passes. AssetSource supplies the logical inventory and a standard Read reader for each selected payload. The provider decides how to obtain those bytes. Filesystem path safety and HTTP response handling belong to the relevant adapter or library, not to the content checks. A future provider can implement the same interface without adding a new retrieval mode to the verifier. verify_payload_into uses standard I/O to stream into a writer while the course code counts bytes and updates the digest. For a selected 3-byte payload, it observes at most 4 bytes: the fourth distinguishes a complete 3-byte stream from a longer stream with the same prefix. That excess byte is not written to the destination. A short stream fails with Size; so does an overrun. Equal-length content with the wrong digest fails with Hash. A reader or writer failure is Io, not successful end of input. Rust compares streamed content with the selected byte count and digest, observes one possible excess byte, and keeps any failed write provisional. rust/crates/llm-from-scratch/src/artifact/inventory.rs#bounded-payload-verification struct CheckingWriter<'a, W: ?Sized> { sink: &'a mut W, hash: Sha256, bytes: u64, limit: u64, oversized: bool, } impl<W: Write + ?Sized> Write for CheckingWriter<'_, W> { fn write(&mut self, chunk: &[u8]) -> std::io::Result<usize> { let retained = (chunk.len() as u64).min(self.limit - self.bytes) as usize; self.sink.write_all(&chunk[..retained])?; self.hash.update(&chunk[..retained]); self.bytes += retained as u64; if retained != chunk.len() { self.oversized = true; return Err(std::io::Error::new( std::io::ErrorKind::InvalidData, \"content exceeds selected size\", )); } Ok(retained) } fn flush(&mut self) -> std::io::Result<()> { self.sink.flush() } } /// Standard I/O performs streaming and propagates backend failures. The course /// compares the selected length and digest, and never writes the excess byte /// used to distinguish a true EOF from a same-prefix oversize stream. /// The sink can contain an unverified prefix on failure. Its owner must keep /// that prefix private; this function does not roll back arbitrary writers. pub fn verify_payload_into<R: Read + ?Sized, W: Write + ?Sized>( expected: &PayloadEntry, reader: &mut R, sink: &mut W, ) -> Result<VerifiedPayload, AcquisitionError> { let read_limit = expected .bytes .checked_add(1) .ok_or(AcquisitionError::Size)?; let mut checked = CheckingWriter { sink: &mut *sink, hash: Sha256::new(), bytes: 0, limit: expected.bytes, oversized: false, }; let copied = std::io::copy(&mut reader.take(read_limit), &mut checked); if checked.oversized { return Err(AcquisitionError::Size); } copied.map_err(|_| AcquisitionError::Io)?; if checked.bytes != expected.bytes { return Err(AcquisitionError::Size); } let digest = format!(\"{:x}\", checked.hash.finalize()); if digest != expected.sha256 { return Err(AcquisitionError::Hash); } sink.flush().map_err(|_| AcquisitionError::Io)?; Ok(VerifiedPayload { id: expected.id.clone(), bytes: expected.bytes, sha256: digest, }) } pub fn verify_payload<R: Read + ?Sized>( expected: &PayloadEntry, reader: &mut R, ) -> Result<VerifiedPayload, AcquisitionError> { verify_payload_into(expected, reader, &mut std::io::sink()) } SHA-256 and JSON syntax use supporting libraries. Course Rust owns record consistency, canonical ordering, selected-policy agreement, logical inventory and the comparisons that decide admission. Keep incomplete content out of the published bundle AssetStore creates a private stage with standard Write writers. A writer may contain an unverified prefix when verification fails. Such bytes must remain unpublished; the caller must not treat them as an admitted payload. acquire_bundle verifies each payload, finishes it in the private stage, and calls publish only after the entire bundle passes. The storage adapter owns atomic publication, durability and cleanup. The content algorithm does not assume a directory layout, reserved manifest filename or database protocol. The example uses a memory store. Its failed replacement leaves the prior bundle unchanged and publishes no partial candidate. This demonstrates the admission order and this store’s behavior, not crash durability for every possible storage backend. An adapter must publish a complete bundle or none of it; a storage error after publication may leave a complete bundle visible and must not be described as proof of rollback. Rust stages selected payloads privately and requests publication only after every length and digest check succeeds; the store owns atomic visibility and durability. rust/crates/llm-from-scratch/src/artifact/acquisition.rs#content-admission pub fn acquire_bundle<S: AssetSource, D: AssetStore>( manifest: &DatasetArtifactManifestV2, policy: &DatasetPolicy, source: &mut S, destination: &mut D, ) -> Result<VerifiedBundle, AcquisitionError> { admit_inventory(manifest, policy, source)?; let manifest_bytes = canonical_manifest_bytes(manifest)?; let mut stage = destination.stage(manifest)?; let mut verified = Vec::with_capacity(manifest.payload.len()); for expected in &manifest.payload { let mut reader = source.open_payload(expected)?; let mut writer = stage.create_payload(expected)?; let payload = verify_payload_into(expected, &mut reader, &mut writer)?; stage.finish_payload(expected, writer)?; verified.push(payload); } let proof = bundle_proof(manifest, policy, verified)?; stage.publish(&manifest_bytes, &proof)?; Ok(proof) } Two changes that expose the boundary Replacing b\"abc\" with b\"abd\" preserves the training payload’s 3-byte length. A byte-count check accepts the replacement, but the full verifier returns Hash. This identifies a content mismatch, not what either text would teach an LLM. For a separate deliberate selection, change attribution to b\"course-authored fixture v2\\n\". Its payload entry now records 27 bytes and a different digest. The source records still refer to the same logical attribution ID; the raw text digests remain unchanged. The new complete payload totals 49 bytes, and its canonical manifest has a different identity. The original policy refuses this variant until the caller independently selects the new record; changing supplied metadata does not authorize itself. replay_bundle reads a canonical manifest, checks the selected artifact identity and verifies every currently supplied payload again. It has no destination-writing interface. Matching an old identity alone would not detect payload bytes changed afterward. The executable prints a report with scope synthetic-offline-fixture, including all payload counts and digests, the attribution comparison, complete replay and the preserved prior bundle. These are checked toy results, not acquisition of a training dataset. The synthetic Rust report distinguishes corpus-record identity, verified payload bytes, complete replay and the memory store's failed-replacement result. rust/demos/ch41-governed-corpus-acquisition/src/lib.rs#governed-report Ok(serde_json::json!({ \"artifact_id\": verified.artifact_id(), \"artifact_manifest_bytes\": canonical_manifest_bytes(&manifest)?.len(), \"attribution_variant_artifact_id\": artifact_id(&variant)?.as_hex(), \"checks\": { \"attribution_change_changes_bundle_identity\": artifact_id(&manifest)? != artifact_id(&variant)?, \"attribution_change_preserves_raw_digests\": manifest.payload.iter().filter(|entry| entry.role.starts_with(\"raw-\")).all(|entry| variant.payload.iter().any(|other| other.id == entry.id && other.sha256 == entry.sha256)), \"complete_bundle_replay_identity\": replay == verified, \"failure_preserves_prior_bundle\": refusal == AcquisitionError::Hash && prior.bundles == last_good, \"same_size_wrong_bytes_refusal\": corrupt.to_string(), \"size_only_contrast_accepts_abd\": size_only_accepts(train.bytes, b\"abd\") }, \"inventoried_payloads\": verified.payloads().len(), \"logical_sources\": manifest.sources.len(), \"payloads\": verified.payloads().iter().map(|entry| serde_json::json!({\"bytes\":entry.bytes(),\"id\":entry.id(),\"sha256\":entry.sha256()})).collect::<Vec<_>>(), \"privacy_quality_or_redistribution_approval\": false, \"raw_bytes\": 9, \"schema_version\": 2, \"scope\": policy.evidence_kind(), \"total_payload_bytes\": verified.total_bytes() })) Run the demo from the repository root, the directory containing course, with Docker installed and running. Set COURSE_CORPUS=false because this example uses only its tiny built-in inputs, not the optional large corpus. If the workspace image is absent, the wrapper first builds it using network access for dependencies; the demo itself then runs with network access disabled: COURSE_CORPUS=false ./course run cargo run --offline --locked -p ch41-governed-corpus-acquisition The command prints the JSON report described above, with 2 logical sources, 4 verified payloads, 9 raw bytes and 46 total payload bytes. A source uses that name to refer to content; adapters choose how to retrieve or store it. The name is not a required filename or URL. Corpus bundle The selected raw text and metadata payloads together with their manifest. In this synthetic example, two sources share one license payload and one attribution payload. Dataset artifact identity The SHA-256 digest of the complete canonical manifest. It identifies the record through its provenance and payload digests; supplied payload bytes still need verification. It is not a signature or permission certificate. Raw held-out source The separate raw text source selected outside the raw training source. Its name does not define the final validation or test split, which is constructed later. Source provenance The record connecting selected corpus content to its source revision, provenance reference, license text and attribution. reading.roleRequirement: Explain why filenames, retrieved text and source labels alone do not identify the selected training corpus; establish the need for content plus provenance agreement independently of retrieval/storage and exclude cleaning, privacy, permission and training quality.
reading.value: The problem: available text does not identify a training corpus An LLM learns from the text supplied to its training pipeline. A filename alone does not identify that text: two files named train.txt can contain different bytes. A source can also change between revisions. Even the intended text is an incomplete corpus record if its source revision, license text or attribution has been lost. Before filtering or tokenizing, we need to connect the selected text to its documented origin and check that the supplied bytes match that selection. The same check should work whether those bytes arrive from a file, an HTTP client or another reader, and whether the verified bundle is kept in memory, files or another store. How bytes travel and where they are kept do not change which content was selected. This chapter implements that content boundary. Verification does not clean the text, establish privacy, grant legal permission or measure its usefulness for training.

reading.value:
Start with a complete, tiny corpus bundle The example uses course-authored test bytes, not a downloaded training dataset. A payload is one byte sequence included in the bundle. A content ID is its logical name within the selected record, not a filename or a URL. Content ID | Role in this fixture | Exact bytes as a Rust literal | Byte count train | Raw training source | b"abc" | 3 validation | Raw held-out source | b"hello
" | 6 license | Shared license text | b"fixture-only
" | 13 attribution | Shared attribution text | b"course-authored fixture
" | 24 In these literals,

Both source records refer to the same license and attribution payloads; shared bytes are inventoried once. The fixture’s license identifier is LicenseRef-Course-Test-Only, and its redistribution labels are not-approved. These describe the synthetic record, not permission for a real corpus or a trained model. The held-out source is raw input; its name does not define the final validation or test split.

reading.roleRequirement: Explain manifest payload/source fields and independently selected policy authority; distinguish descriptive provenance from retrieval instructions and self-consistency from intended-corpus agreement. State variable selected counts and exact canonical ordering/format before the complete-record identity formula.
reading.value: The solution: select the record, then verify its content A manifest records the bundle. Each payload entry supplies a content ID, role, media type, exact byte count and SHA-256 digest. Each source record names the corresponding content ID, source revision, provenance reference, license and attribution. The provenance reference is descriptive evidence; it need not be a URL and is not an instruction to fetch anything. The caller must select the expected record independently of the candidate being checked. Rust’s DatasetPolicy stores that selection. Copying an untrusted candidate into the expected policy would check only its internal consistency, not whether it was the intended corpus. The verifier cannot make the caller’s provenance claims true merely by matching them. For this tiny example, the selected record contains 2 sources and 4 payloads. The reusable verifier does not require those counts. Other selections can name different numbers of sources, share metadata or include additional payloads. The manifest has one canonical representation: compact UTF-8 JSON, object keys sorted by their UTF-8 bytes, payload entries sorted by the UTF-8 bytes of their content IDs, source entries sorted by the UTF-8 bytes of their source IDs, and exactly one final newline. An incoming manifest with different formatting or ordering is rejected, not silently rewritten. This fixes the exact bytes used for identity: \mathrm{artifact\_id}=\operatorname{SHA256}(\mathrm{canonical\_manifest\_bytes})

reading.roleRequirement: Define the identity formula's exact record bytes, SHA256 operation,256-bit digest and64-character display; distinguish recorded payload digests from current-byte verification and exclude signature, permission, privacy and quality certification.
reading.value: What the identity formula means Here \mathrm{canonical\_manifest\_bytes} is the complete canonical record, including payload digests and provenance. \operatorname{SHA256} maps those bytes to a 256-bit digest. \mathrm{artifact\_id} is that digest, displayed as 64 hexadecimal characters. It identifies a record; it is not a signature or a permission, privacy or quality certificate. Payload bytes affect the identity through their recorded counts and digests. The verifier must still read the actual payloads. Hashing a manifest does not prove that its claimed content exists. Rust identifies the complete corpus record by hashing its exact canonical manifest bytes; the payloads still require verification. rust/crates/llm-from-scratch/src/artifact/canonical_manifest.rs#dataset-artifact-identity pub fn artifact_id( manifest: &DatasetArtifactManifestV2, ) -> Result<ArtifactDigest, AcquisitionError> { Ok(sha256(&canonical_manifest_bytes(manifest)?)) }

reading.roleRequirement: Teach policy→exact logical inventory→all-payload verification order, standard Read/Write providers and adapter-owned retrieval/storage, selected-size-plus-one EOF checking, Size/Hash/Io failures and provisional writes. Explain complete staged publication, bounded memory-store failure evidence, separately selected attribution variation, current-byte replay and runnable offline toy commands with truthful image preparation context.
reading.value: Verify supplied bytes without choosing their transport The content verifier performs three checks in order: Validate the candidate manifest’s structure and require exact agreement with the independently selected policy, including its provenance and producer identifiers. Require the provider’s logical inventory to match the selected payload IDs exactly. A missing, extra or duplicate ID causes refusal before payloads are opened or destination staging is created. Read every selected payload through standard Rust I/O. Compare its observed length and digest with its selected entry. Accept the bundle only after every payload passes. AssetSource supplies the logical inventory and a standard Read reader for each selected payload. The provider decides how to obtain those bytes. Filesystem path safety and HTTP response handling belong to the relevant adapter or library, not to the content checks. A future provider can implement the same interface without adding a new retrieval mode to the verifier. verify_payload_into uses standard I/O to stream into a writer while the course code counts bytes and updates the digest. For a selected 3-byte payload, it observes at most 4 bytes: the fourth distinguishes a complete 3-byte stream from a longer stream with the same prefix. That excess byte is not written to the destination. A short stream fails with Size; so does an overrun. Equal-length content with the wrong digest fails with Hash. A reader or writer failure is Io, not successful end of input. Rust compares streamed content with the selected byte count and digest, observes one possible excess byte, and keeps any failed write provisional. rust/crates/llm-from-scratch/src/artifact/inventory.rs#bounded-payload-verification struct CheckingWriter<'a, W: ?Sized> { sink: &'a mut W, hash: Sha256, bytes: u64, limit: u64, oversized: bool, } impl<W: Write + ?Sized> Write for CheckingWriter<'_, W> { fn write(&mut self, chunk: &[u8]) -> std::io::Result<usize> { let retained = (chunk.len() as u64).min(self.limit - self.bytes) as usize; self.sink.write_all(&chunk[..retained])?; self.hash.update(&chunk[..retained]); self.bytes += retained as u64; if retained != chunk.len() { self.oversized = true; return Err(std::io::Error::new( std::io::ErrorKind::InvalidData, "content exceeds selected size", )); } Ok(retained) } fn flush(&mut self) -> std::io::Result<()> { self.sink.flush() } } /// Standard I/O performs streaming and propagates backend failures. The course /// compares the selected length and digest, and never writes the excess byte /// used to distinguish a true EOF from a same-prefix oversize stream. /// The sink can contain an unverified prefix on failure. Its owner must keep /// that prefix private; this function does not roll back arbitrary writers. pub fn verify_payload_into<R: Read + ?Sized, W: Write + ?Sized>( expected: &PayloadEntry, reader: &mut R, sink: &mut W, ) -> Result<VerifiedPayload, AcquisitionError> { let read_limit = expected .bytes .checked_add(1) .ok_or(AcquisitionError::Size)?; let mut checked = CheckingWriter { sink: &mut *sink, hash: Sha256::new(), bytes: 0, limit: expected.bytes, oversized: false, }; let copied = std::io::copy(&mut reader.take(read_limit), &mut checked); if checked.oversized { return Err(AcquisitionError::Size); } copied.map_err(|_| AcquisitionError::Io)?; if checked.bytes != expected.bytes { return Err(AcquisitionError::Size); } let digest = format!("{:x}", checked.hash.finalize()); if digest != expected.sha256 { return Err(AcquisitionError::Hash); } sink.flush().map_err(|_| AcquisitionError::Io)?; Ok(VerifiedPayload { id: expected.id.clone(), bytes: expected.bytes, sha256: digest, }) } pub fn verify_payload<R: Read + ?Sized>( expected: &PayloadEntry, reader: &mut R, ) -> Result<VerifiedPayload, AcquisitionError> { verify_payload_into(expected, reader, &mut std::io::sink()) } SHA-256 and JSON syntax use supporting libraries. Course Rust owns record consistency, canonical ordering, selected-policy agreement, logical inventory and the comparisons that decide admission. Keep incomplete content out of the published bundle AssetStore creates a private stage with standard Write writers. A writer may contain an unverified prefix when verification fails. Such bytes must remain unpublished; the caller must not treat them as an admitted payload. acquire_bundle verifies each payload, finishes it in the private stage, and calls publish only after the entire bundle passes. The storage adapter owns atomic publication, durability and cleanup. The content algorithm does not assume a directory layout, reserved manifest filename or database protocol. The example uses a memory store. Its failed replacement leaves the prior bundle unchanged and publishes no partial candidate. This demonstrates the admission order and this store’s behavior, not crash durability for every possible storage backend. An adapter must publish a complete bundle or none of it; a storage error after publication may leave a complete bundle visible and must not be described as proof of rollback. Rust stages selected payloads privately and requests publication only after every length and digest check succeeds; the store owns atomic visibility and durability. rust/crates/llm-from-scratch/src/artifact/acquisition.rs#content-admission pub fn acquire_bundle<S: AssetSource, D: AssetStore>( manifest: &DatasetArtifactManifestV2, policy: &DatasetPolicy, source: &mut S, destination: &mut D, ) -> Result<VerifiedBundle, AcquisitionError> { admit_inventory(manifest, policy, source)?; let manifest_bytes = canonical_manifest_bytes(manifest)?; let mut stage = destination.stage(manifest)?; let mut verified = Vec::with_capacity(manifest.payload.len()); for expected in &manifest.payload { let mut reader = source.open_payload(expected)?; let mut writer = stage.create_payload(expected)?; let payload = verify_payload_into(expected, &mut reader, &mut writer)?; stage.finish_payload(expected, writer)?; verified.push(payload); } let proof = bundle_proof(manifest, policy, verified)?; stage.publish(&manifest_bytes, &proof)?; Ok(proof) } Two changes that expose the boundary Replacing b"abc" with b"abd" preserves the training payload’s 3-byte length. A byte-count check accepts the replacement, but the full verifier returns Hash. This identifies a content mismatch, not what either text would teach an LLM. For a separate deliberate selection, change attribution to b"course-authored fixture v2\n". Its payload entry now records 27 bytes and a different digest. The source records still refer to the same logical attribution ID; the raw text digests remain unchanged. The new complete payload totals 49 bytes, and its canonical manifest has a different identity. The original policy refuses this variant until the caller independently selects the new record; changing supplied metadata does not authorize itself. replay_bundle reads a canonical manifest, checks the selected artifact identity and verifies every currently supplied payload again. It has no destination-writing interface. Matching an old identity alone would not detect payload bytes changed afterward. The executable prints a report with scope synthetic-offline-fixture, including all payload counts and digests, the attribution comparison, complete replay and the preserved prior bundle. These are checked toy results, not acquisition of a training dataset. The synthetic Rust report distinguishes corpus-record identity, verified payload bytes, complete replay and the memory store's failed-replacement result. rust/demos/ch41-governed-corpus-acquisition/src/lib.rs#governed-report Ok(serde_json::json!({ "artifact_id": verified.artifact_id(), "artifact_manifest_bytes": canonical_manifest_bytes(&manifest)?.len(), "attribution_variant_artifact_id": artifact_id(&variant)?.as_hex(), "checks": { "attribution_change_changes_bundle_identity": artifact_id(&manifest)? != artifact_id(&variant)?, "attribution_change_preserves_raw_digests": manifest.payload.iter().filter(|entry| entry.role.starts_with("raw-")).all(|entry| variant.payload.iter().any(|other| other.id == entry.id && other.sha256 == entry.sha256)), "complete_bundle_replay_identity": replay == verified, "failure_preserves_prior_bundle": refusal == AcquisitionError::Hash && prior.bundles == last_good, "same_size_wrong_bytes_refusal": corrupt.to_string(), "size_only_contrast_accepts_abd": size_only_accepts(train.bytes, b"abd") }, "inventoried_payloads": verified.payloads().len(), "logical_sources": manifest.sources.len(), "payloads": verified.payloads().iter().map(|entry| serde_json::json!({"bytes":entry.bytes(),"id":entry.id(),"sha256":entry.sha256()})).collect::<Vec<_>>(), "privacy_quality_or_redistribution_approval": false, "raw_bytes": 9, "schema_version": 2, "scope": policy.evidence_kind(), "total_payload_bytes": verified.total_bytes() })) Run the demo from the repository root, the directory containing course, with Docker installed and running. Set COURSE_CORPUS=false because this example uses only its tiny built-in inputs, not the optional large corpus. If the workspace image is absent, the wrapper first builds it using network access for dependencies; the demo itself then runs with network access disabled: COURSE_CORPUS=false ./course run cargo run --offline --locked -p ch41-governed-corpus-acquisition The command prints the JSON report described above, with 2 logical sources, 4 verified payloads, 9 raw bytes and 46 total payload bytes. Its same_size_wrong_bytes_refusal is Hash, and failure_preserves_prior_bundle is true. The executable runs the course-authored offline corpus fixture and prints its checked report; it does not download a corpus. rust/demos/ch41-governed-corpus-acquisition/src/main.rs#offline-acquisition-example fn main() -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> { // The executable has no HTTP transport and no production acquisition mode. let report = run_fixture()?; println!("{}", serde_json::to_string_pretty(&report)?); Ok(()) }

Datasheets for Datasets proposes structured dataset documentation; the later ROOTS corpus describes data creation, curation and governance for a multilingual language-model corpus. Datasheets for Datasets, first posted in 2018 and revised in the linked 2021 version, provides the earlier example. Gebru and colleagues propose dataset documentation describing motivation, composition, collection and recommended uses to improve communication, transparency and accountability. A checksum cannot replace those informed judgments. The BigScience ROOTS Corpus is described in a 2023 preprint. The ROOTS corpus paper documents data creation and curation with governance foregrounded in a multilingual language-model project; it does not validate this chapter’s fixture. import RustSource from "../../../components/RustSource.astro";

{/* chapter-section:worked-example */}

## The problem: available text does not identify a training corpus

An LLM learns from the text supplied to its training pipeline. A filename alone
does not identify that text: two files named `train.txt` can contain different
bytes. A source can also change between revisions. Even the intended text is an
incomplete corpus record if its source revision, license text or attribution
has been lost.

Before filtering or tokenizing, we need to connect the selected text to its
documented origin and check that the supplied bytes match that selection. The
same check should work whether those bytes arrive from a file, an HTTP client
or another reader, and whether the verified bundle is kept in memory, files or
another store. How bytes travel and where they are kept do not change which
content was selected.

This chapter implements that content boundary. Verification does not clean the
text, establish privacy, grant legal permission or measure its usefulness for
training.

## Start with a complete, tiny corpus bundle

The example uses course-authored test bytes, not a downloaded training dataset.
A **payload** is one byte sequence included in the bundle. A **content ID** is
its logical name within the selected record, not a filename or a URL.

| Content ID | Role in this fixture | Exact bytes as a Rust literal | Byte count |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `train` | Raw training source | `b"abc"` | $3$ |
| `validation` | Raw held-out source | `b"hello\n"` | $6$ |
| `license` | Shared license text | `b"fixture-only\n"` | $13$ |
| `attribution` | Shared attribution text | `b"course-authored fixture\n"` | $24$ |

In these literals, `\n` represents one newline byte. The raw text contains
$3+6=9$ bytes. The complete payload contains $3+6+13+24=46$ bytes, excluding
the manifest introduced below. Both source records refer to the same license
and attribution payloads; shared bytes are inventoried once.

The fixture's license identifier is `LicenseRef-Course-Test-Only`, and its
redistribution labels are `not-approved`. These describe the synthetic record,
not permission for a real corpus or a trained model. The held-out source is raw
input; its name does not define the final validation or test split.

{/* chapter-section:formula */}

## The solution: select the record, then verify its content

A **manifest** records the bundle. Each payload entry supplies a content ID,
role, media type, exact byte count and SHA-256 digest. Each source record names
the corresponding content ID, source revision, provenance reference, license
and attribution. The provenance reference is descriptive evidence; it need not
be a URL and is not an instruction to fetch anything.

The caller must select the expected record independently of the candidate
being checked. Rust's `DatasetPolicy` stores that selection. Copying an
untrusted candidate into the expected policy would check only its internal
consistency, not whether it was the intended corpus. The verifier cannot make
the caller's provenance claims true merely by matching them.

For this tiny example, the selected record contains $2$ sources and $4$ payloads.
The reusable verifier does not require those counts. Other selections can name
different numbers of sources, share metadata or include additional payloads.

The manifest has one **canonical** representation: compact UTF-8 JSON, object
keys sorted by their UTF-8 bytes, payload entries sorted by the UTF-8 bytes of
their content IDs, source entries sorted by the UTF-8 bytes of their source IDs,
and exactly one final newline. An incoming manifest
with different formatting or ordering is rejected, not silently rewritten.
This fixes the exact bytes used for identity:

$$
\mathrm{artifact\_id}=\operatorname{SHA256}(\mathrm{canonical\_manifest\_bytes})
$$

{/* chapter-section:symbol-glossary */}

## What the identity formula means

Here $\mathrm{canonical\_manifest\_bytes}$ is the complete canonical record,
including payload digests and provenance. $\operatorname{SHA256}$ maps those
bytes to a $256$-bit digest. $\mathrm{artifact\_id}$ is that digest, displayed
as $64$ hexadecimal characters. It identifies a record; it is not a signature
or a permission, privacy or quality certificate.

Payload bytes affect the identity through their recorded counts and digests.
The verifier must still read the actual payloads. Hashing a manifest does not
prove that its claimed content exists.

<RustSource
  path="rust/crates/llm-from-scratch/src/artifact/canonical_manifest.rs"
  region="dataset-artifact-identity"
  caption="Rust identifies the complete corpus record by hashing its exact canonical manifest bytes; the payloads still require verification."
  label="Rust source: identity of the canonical corpus record"
/>

{/* chapter-section:rust-implementation */}

## Verify supplied bytes without choosing their transport

The content verifier performs three checks in order:

1. Validate the candidate manifest's structure and require exact agreement with
   the independently selected policy, including its provenance and producer
   identifiers.
2. Require the provider's logical inventory to match the selected payload IDs
   exactly. A missing, extra or duplicate ID causes refusal before payloads are
   opened or destination staging is created.
3. Read every selected payload through standard Rust I/O. Compare its observed
   length and digest with its selected entry. Accept the bundle only after every
   payload passes.

`AssetSource` supplies the logical inventory and a standard `Read` reader for
each selected payload. The provider decides how to obtain those bytes. Filesystem
path safety and HTTP response handling belong to the relevant adapter or library,
not to the content checks. A future provider can implement the same interface
without adding a new retrieval mode to the verifier.

`verify_payload_into` uses standard I/O to stream into a writer while the
course code counts bytes and updates the digest. For a selected $3$-byte payload,
it observes at most $4$ bytes: the fourth distinguishes a complete $3$-byte stream
from a longer stream with the same prefix. That excess byte is not written to
the destination. A short stream fails with `Size`; so does an overrun.
Equal-length content with the wrong digest fails with `Hash`. A reader or
writer failure is `Io`, not successful end of input.

<RustSource
  path="rust/crates/llm-from-scratch/src/artifact/inventory.rs"
  region="bounded-payload-verification"
  caption="Rust compares streamed content with the selected byte count and digest, observes one possible excess byte, and keeps any failed write provisional."
  label="Rust source: streamed corpus-content size and digest checks"
/>

SHA-256 and JSON syntax use supporting libraries. Course Rust owns record
consistency, canonical ordering, selected-policy agreement, logical inventory
and the comparisons that decide admission.

### Keep incomplete content out of the published bundle

`AssetStore` creates a private stage with standard `Write` writers.
A writer may contain an unverified prefix when verification fails. Such bytes
must remain unpublished; the caller must not treat them as an admitted payload.

`acquire_bundle` verifies each payload, finishes it in the private stage,
and calls `publish` only after the entire bundle passes. The storage adapter
owns atomic publication, durability and cleanup. The content algorithm does not
assume a directory layout, reserved manifest filename or database protocol.

The example uses a memory store. Its failed replacement leaves the prior bundle
unchanged and publishes no partial candidate. This demonstrates the admission
order and this store's behavior, not crash durability for every possible storage
backend. An adapter must publish a complete bundle or none of it; a storage error
after publication may leave a complete bundle visible and must not be described
as proof of rollback.

<RustSource
  path="rust/crates/llm-from-scratch/src/artifact/acquisition.rs"
  region="content-admission"
  caption="Rust stages selected payloads privately and requests publication only after every length and digest check succeeds; the store owns atomic visibility and durability."
  label="Rust source: complete corpus-bundle admission into an external store"
/>

### Two changes that expose the boundary

Replacing `b"abc"` with `b"abd"` preserves the training payload's $3$-byte
length. A byte-count check accepts the replacement, but the full verifier returns
`Hash`. This identifies a content mismatch, not what either text would teach
an LLM.

For a separate deliberate selection, change attribution to
`b"course-authored fixture v2\n"`. Its payload entry now records $27$ bytes and
a different digest. The source records still refer to the same logical
attribution ID; the raw text digests remain unchanged. The new complete payload
totals $49$ bytes, and its canonical manifest has a different identity.
The original policy refuses this variant until the caller independently selects
the new record; changing supplied metadata does not authorize itself.

`replay_bundle` reads a canonical manifest, checks the selected artifact
identity and verifies every currently supplied payload again. It has no
destination-writing interface. Matching an old identity alone would not detect
payload bytes changed afterward.

The executable prints a report with scope `synthetic-offline-fixture`,
including all payload counts and digests, the attribution comparison,
complete replay and the preserved prior bundle. These are checked toy results,
not acquisition of a training dataset.

<RustSource
  path="rust/demos/ch41-governed-corpus-acquisition/src/lib.rs"
  region="governed-report"
  caption="The synthetic Rust report distinguishes corpus-record identity, verified payload bytes, complete replay and the memory store's failed-replacement result."
  label="Rust source: verified synthetic corpus-bundle report"
/>

Run the demo from the repository root, the directory containing `course`,
with Docker installed and running. Set `COURSE_CORPUS=false` because this example
uses only its tiny built-in inputs, not the optional large corpus. If the workspace
image is absent, the wrapper first builds it using network access for dependencies;
the demo itself then runs with network access disabled:

```sh
COURSE_CORPUS=false ./course run cargo run --offline --locked -p ch41-governed-corpus-acquisition
```

The command prints the JSON report described above, with $2$ logical sources,
$4$ verified payloads, $9$ raw bytes and $46$ total payload bytes. Its
`same_size_wrong_bytes_refusal` is `Hash`, and
`failure_preserves_prior_bundle` is `true`.

<RustSource
  path="rust/demos/ch41-governed-corpus-acquisition/src/main.rs"
  region="offline-acquisition-example"
  caption="The executable runs the course-authored offline corpus fixture and prints its checked report; it does not download a corpus."
  label="Rust source: executable offline corpus-verification example"
/>

{/* chapter-section:history */}

## History: preserve dataset context beside the bytes

A byte-count inventory detects missing or truncated content, but equal-length
`abc` and `abd` expose its limit. The following Rust function demonstrates
that narrow baseline; it does not reenact a historical dataset project's full
process.

<RustSource
  path="rust/demos/ch41-governed-corpus-acquisition/src/lib.rs"
  region="size-only-contrast"
  caption="The course-local byte-count baseline accepts both three-byte inputs, abc and abd; it does not establish content identity or provenance."
  label="Rust source: the limited corpus byte-count baseline"
/>

A byte inventory alone does not preserve a dataset's collection context,
provenance or suitability for language-model training.
Datasheets for Datasets proposes structured dataset documentation; the later
ROOTS corpus describes data creation, curation and governance for a multilingual
language-model corpus.

[Datasheets for Datasets](https://arxiv.org/abs/1803.09010v8), first posted in
$2018$ and revised in the linked $2021$ version, provides the earlier example.
Gebru and colleagues propose dataset documentation describing motivation,
composition, collection and recommended uses to improve communication,
transparency and accountability. A checksum cannot replace those informed
judgments.

[The BigScience ROOTS Corpus](https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.03915v1) is described
in a $2023$ preprint. The ROOTS corpus paper documents data creation and curation
with governance foregrounded in a multilingual language-model project; it does
not validate this chapter's fixture. The tiny manifest is not the ROOTS
governance process or proof of corpus suitability.

Keep selected corpus bytes linked to their source context before downstream
filtering, split construction and training. Byte agreement does not establish
quality, privacy or permission. Documentation records context; byte verification
checks agreement with a selection. Neither alone establishes privacy, permission
or training quality.

{/* chapter-section:visualization */}

## Read the evidence directly

A spatial diagram would not clarify these record comparisons. The payload table
states exactly which bytes belong to each role; the Rust report records identity
changes, digest refusal and complete replay directly. Together they distinguish
the selected corpus record, its supplied bytes and the synthetic scope of the
example.

{/* chapter-section:exercises */}

## Optional practice: reproduce and explain the checks

Run each command below from the repository root with Docker installed and
running. Each selected check should report `running 1 test` and
`1 passed; 0 failed`; zero selected tests means the named check did not run.
As with the demo, `COURSE_CORPUS=false` skips the optional corpus during image
preparation; the supported wrapper runs the tests with network disabled.

1. Reproduce the same-size corruption and explain why its length passes but
   its content is refused.

   ```sh
   COURSE_CORPUS=false ./course run cargo test --offline --locked \

   ```

2. Reproduce the attribution-only variant. Identify which payload entry changes

   ```sh
   COURSE_CORPUS=false ./course run cargo test --offline --locked \
     -p ch41-governed-corpus-acquisition \
     --test governed_acquisition \
     provenance_changes_identity_without_changing_raw_digests -- --exact
   ```

3. Reproduce verification and storage failures. Explain why a private candidate
   does not replace the last successfully published memory bundle.

   ```sh
   COURSE_CORPUS=false ./course run cargo test --offline --locked \
     -p ch41-governed-corpus-acquisition \
     --test governed_acquisition \
     failure_preserves_prior_bundle_without_publishing_partial_candidate -- --exact
   ```

<details>
<summary>Checked explanations for the three corpus-content verification tasks</summary>

1. Both `abc` and `abd` contain $3$ bytes, but their digests differ.
   The selected entry expects the digest of `abc`; the verifier returns
   `Hash` for `abd` instead of admitting it as the selected content.
2. Only the attribution payload entry's count and digest change. Both sources
   still refer to content ID `attribution`, and the raw text entries keep
   their original digests. The changed canonical manifest changes the identity.
   The variant needs its own independently selected policy.
3. The test injects a corrupt final payload and separate write, finish and
   publication failures. In each case the memory store keeps the prior bundle
   and publishes no replacement. Earlier verified payloads remain in private
   staging, not in a partially admitted bundle. This is the tested memory-store
   boundary, not a guarantee of crash recovery for arbitrary storage.

</details>

{/* chapter-section:decoder-connection */}

## What this supplies to the decoder pipeline

The scalar reference remains unchanged. This boundary supplies selected,
verified corpus content to later filtering and tokenization. The offline
fixture is not acquired TinyStories or Chapter 42's real input. Real input
needs its own selected provenance and verified bytes; a fixture cannot be
relabeled as training-data acquisition. Quality, privacy, contamination and
final split selection remain separate questions.
